components.name: ControlHints
components.doc: The shell's control hints: a pill that teaches one of the shell's controls at the moment it is useful, beside where it is done, and goes once the person does it. The shell's top layer, over the whole area it is given; it takes no input.

props.name: shows
props.doc: Whether hints show at all: the person's "Show control hints".

props.name: known
props.doc: The hints the person has shown they know, by name.

props.name: shown
props.doc: How often each hint showed, by name.

props.name: search_keys
props.doc: The keys that open search, as the keyboard spells them: what the search hint names.

props.name: touch
props.doc: The person points by touch: hints name what a finger does.

props.name: searching
props.doc: Search is open: the person found it, and a window opened from it is opened from search.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Something has the person's attention (a menu, a sheet, a surface over the windows): no hint begins, and one on screen waits.

props.name: engaged
props.doc: The person is in a call or follows someone: no hint begins, and one on screen goes.

props.name: typing
props.doc: The person is typing (the device's `input.typing`): no hint begins until they pause.

events.name: learn
events.doc: A hint was learned: carries its name.

events.name: show
events.doc: A hint began to show: carries its name.

events.name: withdraw
events.doc: A hint begun never reached the screen, so its showing does not count: carries its name.

components.name: SearchButton
components.doc: The one search affordance an app puts in its chrome: an icon button that opens the platform search over the whole app, or — given the `item` it shows — over that one resource and what it holds (a book's passages, a notebook's notes). It never draws a field, and a window bar that searches for the window takes its place.

props.name: item
props.doc: The resource the search is scoped to, when it is one: the app's search narrowed to it, as the scope pill beside the query reads. Without one, the search reaches everything the app publishes.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the scoped search calls the resource it is narrowed to, in the scope pill: the book's title. The item's own name is read when this is empty.

components.name: ActivityTimeline
components.doc: The history of a document, grouped: runs of typing fold into one band that opens to its changes, each day's changes sit under the day's heading, and a change's menu offers reverting it.

props.name: fill
props.doc: The pane takes the height its parent gives it and scrolls inside, rather than being as tall as its rows inside another scroll.

props.name: newest_first
props.doc: Whether it lists changes newest first.

props.name: day_headings
props.doc: Whether the pane shows the calendar's Today/Yesterday/This week headings.

props.name: people_filters
props.doc: Whether it offers every person and agent in the history as a filter.

parts.name: entries
parts.doc: The changes, oldest first.

events.name: revert
events.doc: A change was reverted: carries the change it is.

events.name: open
events.doc: A change was opened in the app: carries the change it is.

components.name: Autocomplete
components.doc: A field that suggests completions under it as it is typed into: a search over a site's catalogue, a mention, a command.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What to type, shown while it is empty, and what names it to assistive technology.

props.name: max_visible
props.doc: How many suggestion rows show before the list scrolls.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be typed into now.

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: It takes the keyboard as soon as it is in the window, once: a palette that opens to be typed into.

props.name: open_list
props.doc: The rows stand open whenever there are any, instead of opening as the person types or walks them: a palette whose empty field already lists everything.

props.name: tab_groups
props.doc: Tab and Shift+Tab move the highlight to the next group's first row, instead of completing the field to the highlighted row: a palette whose rows are grouped.

props.name: filter
props.doc: The rows narrow to what is typed. Off, the rows are shown as they are offered: a host that already computed them for what is typed, or whose ranking is fuzzier than a substring.

props.name: kinds
props.doc: The kinds of result the rows can be narrowed to, in the order their chips stand over them (a kind's name, as the rows are grouped by it). Empty offers no chips.

props.name: chosen
props.doc: The kinds whose chips are chosen. Empty narrows nothing.

props.name: status
props.doc: A line shown under the field while there are no rows ("Searching…", "Nothing matches").

parts.name: suggestions
parts.doc: The completions to offer, in order.

events.name: change
events.doc: The field's text after each edit: what the host reads as the person types. Carries the text alone; taking a row or the text is [`Self::accept`].

events.name: accept
events.doc: The person took a suggestion, or the text they typed: carries what the field holds now.

events.name: alternate
events.doc: The person took a row with a modifier held: the row's value, and the way they opened it (`here` for Shift, `beside` for Ctrl, `more` for Alt), as `"<way>\t<value>"`.

events.name: filter_kind
events.doc: The person pressed the chip of a kind: carries the kind's name.

events.name: adjust
events.doc: The person stepped the selected row's value: the step (`1` up, `-1` down) and the row's value, as `"<delta>\t<value>"`. Left and Right step a row its host marks adjustable while it is selected.

events.name: cancel
events.doc: The person dismissed the list, keeping nothing.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The text typed, and where the edit of it goes.

components.name: Avatar
components.doc: Who someone is, at a glance: their picture, or their initials on their own colour.

props.name: who
props.doc: The person or agent it shows.

props.name: name
props.doc: What it is called when it shows no one: a group, a thing.

props.name: glyph
props.doc: A glyph instead of initials, on a neutral square: a group, an app.

props.name: square
props.doc: A square rather than a circle: an account or a site, not a person.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: An empty avatar placeholder: a message that continues its author's run lines up under the first one's avatar without repeating it.

props.name: picture
props.doc: Where the person's picture is: a content address (`tilo-blob://<hash>`) or a `data:` address a record carries, read as `ui.Image` reads one. The initials show until it is here.

props.name: colour
props.doc: The presence colour it wears, `rrggbb`, where the workspace assigned one: the colour the member row carries, which is not always the one its identity derives.

props.name: status
props.doc: How they are: `online`, `away`, `busy` or `offline`, drawn as the dot on their face.

props.name: call
props.doc: They are in a call now: an arc sweeps round the ring their face wears, or, where motion is reduced, the ring is lit and still.

components.name: Backdrop
components.doc: What stands under everything a view draws: the shell's wallpaper, the ground of a surface the system itself draws before anything else (setup), or a scrim that dims what it covers.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it shows, for assistive technology; empty reads as nothing.

props.name: ground
props.doc: Which ground it is: the wallpaper unless said.

components.name: Badge
components.doc: A small pill on another element: how many new things there are, a dot for something new, a short status ("Owner", "Beta"), or the mark of unsaved changes.

props.name: text
props.doc: A short status in a word: "Owner", "Beta".

props.name: count
props.doc: How many new things there are, in your colour: nothing at 0, "99+" past 99.

props.name: dot
props.doc: Something new, without a number: a dot in your colour.

props.name: modified
props.doc: Unsaved changes: a dot in the primary ink, which is nobody's and not new.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status the pill means, washed into it.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace a changed count plays at: the theme's unless it says otherwise.

components.name: Banner
components.doc: A message that stays until it is resolved or dismissed: "You're offline", "Storage is almost full". Shows an optional app name, a title, an optional message, up to two actions and a dismiss button. Its kind sets the icon and colour.

props.name: title
props.doc: What happened, in a short sentence.

props.name: message
props.doc: What it means or what to do, under the title.

props.name: source
props.doc: The app's name, shown above the title.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What kind of message it is: `neutral` unless said. A warning or an error is announced at once; the others when assistive technology is idle.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph instead of the kind's own.

props.name: action
props.doc: The label of its main action, at its trailing edge: "Retry".

props.name: secondary_action
props.doc: The label of a second action, before the main one: "Details".

props.name: bare
props.doc: It draws no card of its own: the panel it stands on draws the card, and the banner's words and controls go on that panel's ground (a notification banner in the shell's corner).

events.name: act
events.doc: Its main action was pressed.

events.name: secondary_act
events.doc: Its second action was pressed.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: Its dismiss button was pressed: stop showing it. A banner with this has the button, and closes as it is pressed.

components.name: Board
components.doc: Cards in lists, side by side: a kanban board, a pipeline, tasks by status.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the board is, for assistive technology.

parts.name: lists
parts.doc: The lists, in order.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.doc: Where a page is, as the path to it: each place it is in, a chevron between them, the page itself last.

props.name: root_icon
props.doc: A glyph before the first place: a drive, Home.

parts.name: segments
parts.doc: The places, outermost first; the last is the page itself, which is not pressed.

events.name: edit
events.doc: The empty space after the last place was pressed: offer the path as a field to type in.

components.name: Button
components.doc: A button: pressing it does one thing.

props.name: label
props.doc: What pressing it does, in a word or two.

props.name: accessible_name
props.doc: How assistive technology names it, where that says more than the label shows: the charge reads "61%" beside its charging glyph and is named "61%, charging".

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the label, or instead of it when `icon_only`.

props.name: icon_only
props.doc: Show only the icon, the label naming the button to assistive technology.

props.name: faces
props.doc: Who is here, as their faces: up to three faces, then a face counting the rest, and nothing else on the button at any width. Each is the member, so their face wears the picture they set.

props.name: follows_you
props.doc: The first of `faces` follows the person looking: their face wears the follower's mark — a disc in their colour with an eye, on the face's own edge — beside nothing else, never a count's dot, which says something new is behind a control.

props.name: role
props.doc: What kind of action it is: `secondary` unless said, `plain` for an icon-only one.

props.name: toggled
props.doc: A toggle button, and whether it is on: on, it stands on a lift of its ground and is announced as pressed.

props.name: size
props.doc: How prominent it is: `regular` unless said.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be pressed now.

props.name: opens
props.doc: The moment it can first be pressed, where a rule opens it after a wait: until then it stands dimmed with the time left on its face, and it opens by itself then. A view has no clock, so the button keeps it.

props.name: default_focus
props.doc: Whether it is the answer the surface it stands in starts on: an ask that opens puts the keyboard here, so Enter gives this answer. A view marks the answer its surface opens on, and leaves it off for every other control beside it.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say: the requirement an action does not meet.

props.name: live
props.doc: What it says is news: a screen reader announces it when it appears or changes, without the person moving focus — `polite` waits for a pause, `assertive` speaks at once.

props.name: key
props.doc: The plain key that presses it while its window has the keyboard (and, on a row's action, while that row is selected), as the app declared it (`key: "e"`): the host answers it beside the pressed control's own event. A control of the view's own press shows it beside the label as the keyboard in use spells it; a button for an action keeps its face, its key shown where the action is listed.

props.name: keys
props.doc: The plain keys that press it while its window has the keyboard, each as the app declared it (`keys: ["Right", "Space"]`): every one answers the same press. `key` is the one its keys show; a control that names several usually names none.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many new things wait behind it (unread notifications, new mail), on an icon-only button: a count on its icon's top-trailing corner, as an app icon's does, and nothing at 0.

props.name: dot
props.doc: Something new behind it without a number: a dot on its icon's corner.

props.name: alert
props.doc: It needs the person: the count or the dot in the warning tone, not in your colour.

props.name: in_menu
props.doc: It belongs in its header's menu rather than in the row ([`crate::widget::Button::in_menu`]).

props.name: group
props.doc: The run of its owner's actions it stands in (`group: "Due"`), as the app names it: the header's menu shows rows of one run together, under the run's own row.

events.name: press
events.doc: It was pressed (a click, Enter or Space, an assistive technology).

components.name: CallTile
components.doc: A person in a call at their camera or screen.

props.name: who
props.doc: The person the tile shows, and their face until their picture arrives.

props.name: source
props.doc: What it shows of them: their camera, or the screen they share.

props.name: name
props.doc: What it is called where `who` names nobody the workspace knows (someone a bridge carries in).

props.name: speaking
props.doc: They are heard talking now: their face wears the speaking ring.

props.name: muted
props.doc: Their microphone is off.

components.name: CandlestickChart
components.doc: A price per period as candles: what rose and fell when. Each period is a candle from its open to its close, its wick reaching the period's high and low; a period that closed above its open is drawn in the theme's success ink, one that closed below it in its danger ink, and a flat one dim. The traded volume stands under the prices when shown.

props.name: candles
props.doc: The periods, oldest first: `.candle(label: "Monday", open: 82.0, high: 88.0, low: 80.0, close: 86.0)`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: volume
props.doc: The traded volume under the prices; off unless said.

components.name: Place
components.doc: A resource's view on a canvas: the view on the window surface, with a handle shown over its corner on hover and focus that names it, holds its controls and moves it.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the place shows, as its handle names it and assistive technology reads it.

props.name: carries
props.doc: The resource the place shows, by its published address: what picking the handle up carries, so letting it go on the canvas moves the place and on a composer attaches it.

props.name: target
props.doc: The resource the place shows, whose published actions its menu lists, which the host fills as it fills a `ui.MenuButton`'s: a right-click on the place opens them, and typing there filters them as every context menu does (`canvas.md` §1, "Right-click keeps its menu"). A right-click on content with a menu of its own (a field, a row) is that content's.

parts.name: controls
parts.doc: The handle's controls after the name: the resource's actions, pin and close.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: The view the place shows, filling it.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: The place's menu: the commands the host filled from its target.

components.name: Card
components.doc: A summary of one thing on a surface of its own: a dashboard's tile, a resource's preview.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the card stands for, named in its head.

props.name: accessible_name
props.doc: What assistive technology calls the card, when its title alone does not say it: the title unless given.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many things the card lists, as a count beside its title.

props.name: item
props.doc: The resource the card summarizes.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether it is the selected one among its peers.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: What the card shows, in order.

events.name: activate
events.doc: The card was pressed: open what it stands for.

events.name: hover
events.doc: The pointer came over the card: it is the one under it now.

components.name: CardGrid
components.doc: Cards in equal, aligned columns: the apps of a store, the devices of a network, the paragraphs of a review.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the grid is, for assistive technology.

props.name: card_width
props.doc: How wide a card is at least before the grid drops a column: small, regular or wide objects.

parts.name: cards
parts.doc: The cards, in order.

events.name: select
events.doc: The keyboard moved the selection to a card: carries the item it stands for.

events.name: edit
events.doc: The edit key was pressed on the selected card: carries the item it stands for.

events.name: delete
events.doc: Delete was pressed on the selected card: carries the item it stands for, for the app's destructive action.

components.name: CartesianPlot
components.doc: Readings on numeric axes: a trend over time, a relationship between two measures, a comparison. Each series takes the next colour of the theme's palette and is named in a legend; it draws as a line, an area, steps, points, bars or stems.

props.name: points
props.doc: What is measured, each with its readings: `.points(x: [1.0, 2.0], y: [4.0, 6.0], label: "Latency")`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: x_title
props.doc: What the x axis measures, under it ("Minute", "Distance").

props.name: y_title
props.doc: What the y axis measures, beside it ("Milliseconds").

components.name: BarChart
components.doc: Bars over named categories: how much there is of each, to compare. Several measured things stand beside each other in a category, stack on each other, or stack as shares of the category's whole; each takes the next colour of the theme's palette and is named in a legend.

props.name: bars
props.doc: What is measured, each with its reading in every category: `.bars(values: done, label: "Done")`.

props.name: categories
props.doc: What each group of bars is of, in order, under it: a week, a team, a stage.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: layout
props.doc: How several measured things share a category: `grouped` beside each other unless said, `stacked` on each other, `share` stacked as parts of the category's whole, or `waterfall` for the first measured thing's rises and falls, each standing on the one before.

props.name: readings
props.doc: Each bar's reading written at it.

props.name: unit
props.doc: What a reading counts, written after each value a person pointing at a category reads ("GB", "ms", "/s").

components.name: ChangeMark
components.doc: What someone else changed of a resource that the person looking has not seen yet: who, in which task run, and whether they made, changed or removed it.

props.name: of
props.doc: The resource whose changes it marks.

props.name: by
props.doc: Who made the newest change the person has not seen.

props.name: by_all
props.doc: Everyone who made one of the changes the person has not seen, in the order they changed it (its newest change last), each once.

props.name: said
props.doc: What the newest change did, in the words history says it with ("moved this to").

props.name: noun
props.doc: What one item of it is called, plural ("tasks"): the noun a window's count names.

props.name: noun_one
props.doc: What one item of it is called, singular ("task"): one change names one, so the count and the noun agree in number.

props.name: run
props.doc: The task run it was part of, as its task is titled.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What they did: `created`, `changed` or `removed`.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many changes of it the person has not seen.

props.name: window
props.doc: It marks a window, in its header: it says how many changes and by whom.

props.name: added
props.doc: Every change it counts only put items in (`$noun`): what it says is new rather than changed.

props.name: more
props.doc: The window's document holds more resources than the mark counted: what it says is a lower bound, and says so.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What a window's mark opens: the views of its catch-up (*Since you looked*), placed by whoever placed the mark.

events.name: activate
events.doc: Activated: show what they did, at the run that did it.

components.name: Chart
components.doc: A titled chart of one or more lines over a shared scale, with a grid and the labels of its scale: a history worth reading closely, where a sparkline only hints at a trend.

props.name: series
props.doc: The lines, each over the ones before it: `.series(values: cpu, label: "CPU")`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: max
props.doc: The top of its scale, which may be more than the readings reach; the highest reading unless said.

props.name: area
props.doc: The area under each line washed in its ink.

props.name: top_label
props.doc: The label at the top of its scale: "100%".

props.name: bottom_label
props.doc: The label at the foot of its scale: "0%".

props.name: labels
props.doc: What each reading is at, oldest first ("9:51", "Monday"): the position a person pointing at the chart reads the lines at.

props.name: unit
props.doc: What a reading counts, written after each value read ("ms", "/s").

props.name: height
props.doc: Its height in logical pixels: 160 unless said.

components.name: Sparkline
components.doc: A tiny trend line, with no axis, grid, title or legend: a recent history inside a table cell or a stat card.

props.name: samples
props.doc: The samples, oldest first.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the trend is of, as assistive technology announces it: "Requests per second".

props.name: max
props.doc: The vertical maximum, which may be more than the samples reach; without one it is the highest sample.

props.name: filled
props.doc: The area under the line filled in the same colour, which a sparkline draws unless it is told not to: `true` unless said.

props.name: smooth
props.doc: The line's shape between samples: the smooth curve rather than straight segments.

props.name: leading_dot
props.doc: A dot of this radius on the newest sample: the live edge of a streaming series.

props.name: tone
props.doc: What its line means, when it means something: a status, a person.

props.name: unit
props.doc: What its readings count, written after them in the hover readout ("/s", "h").

components.name: EmojiPicker
components.doc: A button that opens the emoji picker beside it; the emoji picked is reported (`on pick(e)`).

props.name: label
props.doc: What the button is called; "Add reaction" unless it says.

events.name: pick
events.doc: An emoji was picked: carries it.

components.name: Quote
components.doc: A message quoted where another answers it, or in the reply banner over the composer: a rule at its leading edge, who wrote it and the start of what it says.

props.name: excerpt
props.doc: The start of what the quoted message says.

props.name: author
props.doc: Who wrote it.

props.name: caption
props.doc: What the quote is to the message (`Replying to`), shown before the author.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: The close button was pressed.

events.name: activate
events.doc: The quote was pressed: show the message it quotes, or the run of it it names, where that message stands. Without it the quote is read, not pressed.

components.name: Reactions
components.doc: The reactions on something: a pill per emoji with how many reacted, yours drawn on; pressing one adds or takes back your reaction, and the add button opens the emoji picker for another.

props.name: reactions
props.doc: Who reacted, by emoji: the reactions as the message holds them (`Map<Text, Set<Actor>>`).

props.name: emoji
props.doc: The emoji reacted with, in the order they were first used: the older form, with `by`, read while `reactions` is not given.

props.name: by
props.doc: Who reacted with each of `emoji`, in the same order.

props.name: relayed
props.doc: Who reacted with it somewhere else, under a name of their own (a bridged account), each entry its emoji and that name, a tab between them. They stand on the pill of their emoji, counted with the members' reactions, and read as one more name in its tooltip.

props.name: can_react
props.doc: Whether the person may react; they may unless it says not.

events.name: toggle
events.doc: An emoji was pressed or picked: carries it.

events.name: person
events.doc: The face of someone who reacted was chosen: carries who they are, for the view to say more of them (their card).

components.name: Checkbox
components.doc: A box that is marked or not, bound to what it edits (whether to be told of a reply, which rows a bulk action takes).

props.name: label
props.doc: What it is for, beside the box: the whole row chooses it.

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: Some of what it stands for is chosen: a mixed mark.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be chosen now.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace its mark plays at: the theme's unless it says otherwise.

events.name: check
events.doc: It was pressed: what a mark is, in the app's words.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: Whether it is marked, and where a mark made in it goes.

components.name: Chip
components.doc: A compact pill for a tag, a filter or a token: what a note is tagged with, a recipient, an applied filter.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it names, in a word or two.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the label, for a chip that names an action rather than a value.

props.name: faces
props.doc: Who it names, as their face before the label: the member, so their face wears the picture they set, as the bar's faces do. The first is the one shown.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The tone the chip reads in: what it names is a status (a priority, a state of an item), and its pill is washed in that tone.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether the filter it stands for is on; without it the chip is no filter.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be pressed now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside the name, and shown on hover.

props.name: live
props.doc: What it says is news: a screen reader announces it when it appears or changes, without the person moving focus — `polite` waits for a pause, `assertive` speaks at once.

events.name: press
events.doc: It was pressed: open or apply what it names.

events.name: remove
events.doc: Its remove button was pressed: take it away.

components.name: ChordChart
components.doc: How much moves between a set of things: which teams hand work to which, which services call which, which people write to whom. Each thing takes an arc as wide as everything that touches it, a ribbon as wide as its weight joins each pair, and a person pointing at an arc or a ribbon reads what it carries.

props.name: nodes
props.doc: The things it relates, around the ring, in order: `.node(id: "design", label: "Design")`.

props.name: links
props.doc: How much moves between them, in either direction: `.link(from: "design", to: "engineering", value: 32.0)`, `from` and `to` naming nodes by their ids.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, over it and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: Chrome
components.doc: A bar or a dock's body: the theme's bar finish behind what the body holds.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the body is, for assistive technology.

props.name: shape
props.doc: How the body sits in its edge: edge to edge and square (the default), or an inset, rounded body.

props.name: edge
props.doc: The screen edge the body stands on.

props.name: material
props.doc: What the body is made of: the theme's bar body (the default), the theme's glass, or that glass made calm.

props.name: reserve
props.doc: Keep the band the body rests in, and let what it holds grow over it: a dock's item under the pointer stands above the band's edge rather than pushing the band, and the windows under it, up.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: What the body holds.

components.name: Clock
components.doc: A wall clock, live: the time of day in `zone` (the person's when it names none), the day there, and how far its clock stands from here.

props.name: zone
props.doc: The IANA zone (`Asia/Tokyo`) to read the clock in; the person's own when it names none.

props.name: facts
props.doc: Show the day there and how far its clock stands from here, under the time.

props.name: role
props.doc: What the time is, which sets its size and weight: `body` unless said.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: In secondary ink, beside the content it is about.

components.name: CodeEditor
components.doc: Code to read or write, with line numbers and its language's colouring.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What to type, shown while it is empty.

props.name: language
props.doc: The language it colours (the language's own name, `rust`, `json`); plain text unless said.

props.name: min_lines
props.doc: The fewest lines it is tall for.

props.name: max_lines
props.doc: The most lines it is tall for; past them it scrolls.

props.name: gutter
props.doc: The line numbers show.

props.name: read_only
props.doc: It is read and copied, never edited.

props.name: reveal
props.doc: The place to show, written `line` or `line:column` counted from 1; the same place asked for again needs a count after it (`3:1:2`), so a person's own scrolling is left alone.

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How large the code reads, as a factor of its size (`1.25`): the editor's own text zoom, kept by whoever shows it, beside the window's scale rather than instead of it.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The text it edits.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.doc: A colour, picked from a saturation and value field, a hue strip, the red, green and blue sliders, or a hex field; a palette of quick picks sits under them when given.

props.name: swatches
props.doc: A palette of quick picks under the sliders.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many swatches stand in a row.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

events.name: change
events.doc: A colour was picked: carries its hex text.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The colour, as its hex text ("#3a7bd5"), and where a picked colour goes.

components.name: ColorSwatchPicker
components.doc: A grid of swatches, one chosen (a palette of accents): the chosen cell carries the ring.

props.name: swatches
props.doc: The swatches, as hex colours, in order.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many stand in a row.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Which is chosen, counted from 0: none until a person chooses one.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

events.name: change
events.doc: A swatch was chosen: carries its index, counted from 0.

components.name: MenuButton
components.doc: A button that opens a menu of commands under it: a header's More button, a sort menu.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the menu holds, in a word or two. An icon-only button is still named by it.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the label, or instead of it when `icon_only`.

props.name: icon_only
props.doc: Show only the icon, the label naming the button to assistive technology.

props.name: faces
props.doc: Whose menu it is, as their faces in place of the label and icon: the person's own menu on a bar is their face, one person's at an avatar's full size, wearing the picture they set. The label names it to assistive technology.

props.name: role
props.doc: What kind of button it is: `secondary` unless said, `plain` for an icon-only one.

props.name: size
props.doc: How big the button is: `regular` unless said. A bar's button takes the bar's size, so the whole bar grows and shrinks with its setting.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Actions offered on something (`actions(r)`), each a command after `items`.

props.name: target
props.doc: The resource whose published actions this menu lists, which the host fills: a bar that lists the window in front's commands names the window and leaves the commands to it.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: The commands, in order.

components.name: SectionDivider
components.doc: A divider in a conversation: a caption centred in a band, ruled out to both sides, over the row where the part it opens begins — a day of the lines, or the place the reader's unread lines start.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the divider says: the day it opens ("Today", "Sunday", "Jun 21").

props.name: tone
props.doc: What it marks, which sets its ink: a day of the conversation unless said, or the accent where the reader's unread lines start.

components.name: ConversationList
components.doc: A conversation, drawn as every conversation is drawn: each line on its own side, runs of one person's consecutive messages under their name once, a divider where the day changes, and the time and the delivery state under your own.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the conversation is, for assistive technology: "Conversation with Ada".

parts.name: lines
parts.doc: The lines, oldest first.

components.name: Countdown
components.doc: A countdown, live: the time left until `at` — or, once it has come, the time since it — and, with `total`, a ring of how much of it is left.

props.name: at
props.doc: The moment it counts to: the time left until it, or the time since it once it has come.

props.name: total
props.doc: How long the whole is, in seconds: a ring drains as it goes. Without it the readout stands alone, as a stopwatch's does.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the ring measures, under its readout.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large the readout is: `regular` unless said.

components.name: CurveEditor
components.doc: A tone curve a person shapes: a box over the whole range each way, the straight line a plain picture takes, and the points that bend it. A press puts a point where it landed or grabs the one it landed on, a drag bends the curve through it, and letting go well outside the box takes an interior point off again. The line is drawn as the grade applies it, so what is shaped is what the picture gets.

props.name: points
props.doc: The points, a flat list of x and y each in `0..=1`, in ascending x. Both ends are kept at x 0 and x 1; an empty list is the straight line.

props.name: height
props.doc: How tall the box stands, in logical pixels: 160 unless said.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the curve is, for assistive technology: "The red curve".

events.name: change
events.doc: The points moved: carries them all, a flat list of x and y, each `0..=1`.

components.name: DataTable
components.doc: A table of resources as columns and rows: the attributes of a device, the songs in a library, the rules of a firewall.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the table is, for assistive technology.

props.name: fill
props.doc: The table takes the height its parent gives it and scrolls inside itself, rather than being as tall as its rows inside another scroll.

props.name: reserved
props.doc: Rows a finger's target tall, rather than a pointer target and a step.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: Whether pressing a row picks it.

parts.name: columns
parts.doc: The columns, in order.

parts.name: rows
parts.doc: The rows, in order.

events.name: select
events.doc: A row was selected: carries the resource it shows.

events.name: activate
events.doc: A row was activated (a double click, Enter, an assistive technology): carries the resource it shows.

state.name: selection
state.doc: The selected rows, by the resource each stands for.

components.name: DateField
components.doc: A day, shown as the person reads a day (with the time it is due at) and picked from a calendar that opens over it.

props.name: at
props.doc: The time of day the day is due at, when its type pairs one with it (`9:00`): what the chip says after the day.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name: what the date is for.

props.name: optional
props.doc: The date may be cleared: the calendar offers "Clear date".

props.name: compact
props.doc: The field stands beside the entry that tells its day (a moment's field, whose hour the entry types): the chip shows the calendar icon alone, opening the calendar and the time.

parts.name: time
parts.doc: The control that picks the time of day the day is due at: `ui.TimeField(bind: t.at)`.

events.name: change
events.doc: A day was picked, or the date was cleared: carries the moment, or nothing for a cleared one.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The day, as the moment a component binds (its ISO text), and where a picked day goes.

components.name: DatePicker
components.doc: A month's calendar: the day chosen is ringed, today marked, and the arrows go between months.

props.name: marked
props.doc: Days that hold something (an event, a note): a dot under the number.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

events.name: change
events.doc: A day was chosen: carries the moment.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The day chosen, as the moment a component binds (its ISO text), and where choosing one goes.

components.name: DiffGrid
components.doc: Two texts aligned line by line, as a comparison reads: each side's own line numbers, the changed rows washed, and a strip down the side where the changes stand.

props.name: left
props.doc: The left side's lines, one per aligned row: an empty line where it has none.

props.name: right
props.doc: The right side's lines, one per aligned row: an empty line where it has none.

props.name: kinds
props.doc: One character per aligned row: `" "` where both sides hold the same line, `"a"` a line only the right has, `"r"` a line only the left has, `"m"` a line both have and differ.

props.name: at
props.doc: The first row of the change the window is at: the grid brings it into view when it changes.

props.name: side
props.doc: Which side shows: both side by side, or one of them alone where the window is narrow.

props.name: language
props.doc: The language the lines are coloured as (the language's own name, `rust`, `json`); plain text unless said.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the grid shows, as assistive technology announces it: "a.rs and b.rs, 3 changes".

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on a row runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

events.name: press
events.doc: A row was pressed: carries its place among the aligned rows.

events.name: wheel
events.doc: The wheel or the scroll bar asked to show other rows: carries the rows the first one moves by, down for a positive number.

components.name: DisclosureBand
components.doc: Content a view shows only while something is open, unrolling from its top.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What it shows, in order.

components.name: DistributionChart
components.doc: The spread of each measured thing: where its readings centre and how far they run, as a box, a violin or both. Callers give the readings themselves, never quartiles or bins; each series takes the next colour of the theme's palette and is named under the chart.

props.name: samples
props.doc: What was measured, each with the readings taken: `.samples(values: hours, label: "Before")`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: kind
props.doc: How each distribution is drawn: `box` for its quartiles, `violin` for its shape, `both` for the two together unless said.

components.name: Docked
components.doc: Content that fills its column above a bar that stays at the column's foot: a conversation above its composer.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What fills the column; it scrolls itself.

parts.name: foot
parts.doc: The bar at the foot, as tall as it needs.

components.name: DragRun
components.doc: A run of items — a dock's icons, a toolbar's tiles, a row of cards — reordered by dragging one.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the run is, for assistive technology.

props.name: axis
props.doc: Whether the items lead to trailing (the default) or run top to bottom.

props.name: distribute
props.doc: Where the run's packed items sit along it: its leading edge (the default), its centre, its trailing edge, or spread between its ends.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where the items pack across the run: centred (the default).

parts.name: items
parts.doc: The items, in order.

parts.name: trailing
parts.doc: What stands beside the items at the run's trailing end and is never moved: a taskbar's time and device status.

events.name: drop
events.doc: An item was let go in a new place: carries the resource it stands for and its place among the run's other items, from 0 — what `items.move(item, to: at)` takes.

components.name: DragSource
components.doc:
A view a person can pick up and drag: to a drop target in the same window (a search hit, a row of a list, a message's attachment), carrying `resource`, or, given `files`, out of the window as a real file drag another app can take. The ghost under the pointer says `title`.
A press that does not travel is the content's own, so a dragged row still opens when clicked and a dragged chip still presses.

props.name: resource
props.doc: The resource the drag carries, as its published address (`chat.workspace/messages/m1`): what a drop target receives. Empty for a drag of files alone, which leaves the window.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the drag's ghost says under the pointer, and what assistive technology reads instead of the resource's address.

props.name: files
props.doc: The device files the drag offers another app, by path: a press that travels starts the desktop's own drag of them, so a person can drop them into another window. Without them the drag carries its `resource` on this window's drag bus.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What it draws.

events.name: activate
events.doc: It was picked up and let go without travelling: the content's own press did not take it. Reported so a source that wraps something inert still says what happened.

components.name: Drawing
components.doc: Shapes drawn with the design system over a box of their own.

props.name: shapes
props.doc: The shapes, drawn in order, each over the ones before it.

props.name: meaning
props.doc: What it means, for assistive technology and agents.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it shows, as it is announced: "Disk 60% full".

props.name: value
props.doc: How far it has got, for a progress drawing: a fraction.

props.name: width
props.doc: Its width in logical pixels; a square of its height unless said.

props.name: height
props.doc: Its height in logical pixels.

props.name: motion
props.doc: How its shapes move to a new reading: at the theme's pace unless said, never for someone who asked for reduced motion.

props.name: theme
props.doc: The theme its shapes are drawn in, by a shipped theme's id or name (`light`, `paper-dark`, `Tilo light`), so a preview draws a theme other than the running one. Nothing, or a name no shipped theme has, draws them in the running theme.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on it runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

events.name: press
events.doc: The person pressed a shape: carries its index in `shapes`.

events.name: hover
events.doc: The pointer came over a shape, or left them all: carries the index of the shape under it in `shapes`, or none.

events.name: pointer
events.doc: The pointer moved over the drawing, at (x, y): fractions of its box, so the place is the one its shapes are placed at.

events.name: drag_start
events.doc: A drag began over the drawing, at (x, y) in fractions of its box.

events.name: drag
events.doc: The pointer moved while dragging, to (x, y) in fractions of its box.

events.name: drag_end
events.doc: A drag ended at (x, y) in fractions of its box.

events.name: press_at
events.doc: A pointer went down over the drawing, at (x, y) in fractions of its box: the point a person pressed, for a drawing they set things on.

events.name: drag_at
events.doc: The pointer moved over the drawing while pressed, to (x, y) in fractions of its box.

events.name: release_at
events.doc: The pointer came up over the drawing, at (x, y) in fractions of its box.

events.name: wheel
events.doc: The wheel turned over the drawing: across it and down it, in logical pixels, positive down and to the end.

events.name: pinch
events.doc: A pinch over the drawing: the scale factor the fingers ask for, 1 for none.

components.name: DropTarget
components.doc:
A view that takes what another view dragged to it: a chat composer takes an attachment, a dock takes a resource. A drag over it draws the toolkit's drop line, and letting go inside it reports what the drag carried.
It takes a resource dragged out of any [`ui.DragSource`](super::DragSource), a run's item ([`ui.DragItem`](super::DragItem)), and the device files a source of this same window stands for — a file manager's entry let go on a folder's row, even while the desktop carries it. A file dragged in from another application is not taken here, so it is never silently swallowed (`ui.DropZone` and a window's own `drop` are for those).

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What it draws.

events.name: drop
events.doc: A resource was dropped on it: carries the resource the drag carried, as its address, and where inside the target it was let go — its x, then its y, in the target's own logical pixels. The view decides what to do with it — a composer attaches it to the draft, a canvas places it where it was dropped, a shell puts what it holds back there.

events.name: drop_files
events.doc: Device files a source of this window stood for were dropped on it: carries their paths, and where inside the target they were let go, as `drop` says it. A folder's row moves them into its folder.

components.name: DropZone
components.doc: Where files go: dragged here, or chosen with the button.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the zone takes, in a sentence: "Drop files to import".

props.name: message
props.doc: A line under the title saying what it accepts: "PNG or JPEG up to 50 MB".

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph for what it takes, a download arrow unless said.

props.name: action
props.doc: The label of a button offering the same route without dragging ("Choose files").

events.name: drop
events.doc: Files were dropped: each as a `File` — its name, its media type, its size and where its bytes are — kept by the window, which is what an app reads of it.

events.name: choose
events.doc: The action's button was pressed: the view asks for the files its own way.

components.name: Dropdown
components.doc: One of a short list, chosen from a field that opens it: a project, a sort order, a unit.

props.name: options
props.doc: What the list offers, in order.

props.name: values
props.doc: What each option stands for, in order, when it is not the text shown: the list offers the words, and a choice reaches the bound value as its id. Empty makes each option its own value.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What the field says while nothing is chosen, and what names it to assistive technology.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the field: the kind of thing chosen.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A caption above the field.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large the field is: `regular` unless said.

props.name: fill
props.doc: Take the row's width rather than fitting its content.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be chosen from now.

events.name: change
events.doc: A choice was made: carries the chosen option's text.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: What is chosen, and where a choice goes.

components.name: EditableLabel
components.doc: A name typed over where it stands: a document's title, a tab's name, a list item's.

props.name: role
props.doc: What it is set in: `body` unless said.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What it reads, dimmed, while the value is empty: "Untitled".

props.name: edit_on_click
props.doc: Begin an edit on a press, as a document's title does; else on a double click.

props.name: clears_on_blank
props.doc: A blank entry empties the name.

props.name: fill
props.doc: It takes the row's width, eliding a long name.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name, for a label no text beside it names.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the document the window is for, edited in place as its large title.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The name it shows, and where an edit of it goes.

components.name: EmojiPane
components.doc: The emoji picker as a card a view places: search, groups, tones and recents, writing each pick into the field the person was typing in. It is modal while it is open.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether it is open; a closed pane paints nothing and takes no input.

props.name: label
props.doc: What assistive technology calls it; the picker's own card name unless said.

props.name: query
props.doc: The search, where the view types it with keys of its own (an on-screen keyboard's): the card searches for it as if it were typed into its field.

events.name: pick
events.doc: An emoji was picked: carries it.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: It was closed without a pick (Escape, or a press outside it).

components.name: EmptyState
components.doc: What a place says while it holds nothing: a sentence and at most one action.

props.name: title
props.doc: Why it is empty, in one short sentence: "No notes yet".

props.name: message
props.doc: One more sentence under it, when the first does not say enough.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A large glyph above the title: the app's, or the kind of thing that would be here.

props.name: action
props.doc: The label of the one action that fills it: "New note".

props.name: inline
props.doc: Sit within the content, as a list without rows, rather than fill the window.

props.name: error
props.doc: Something failed: the glyph takes the danger colour and the message reads as an error.

events.name: act
events.doc: The action was pressed.

components.name: EnumField
components.doc: A value among an enum's cases: the case it holds, as a chip in the case's glyph and tone, opening the cases to pick another.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the field is for ("Priority"), as the app named it: what a screen reader hears before the case itself.

parts.name: cases
parts.doc: The cases to pick from, in the enum's order.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The case it holds, by the case's name, and where a picked case goes.

components.name: FindControls
components.doc: The window's find controls: the bar's field, the match it stands on of how many, the find's options, the replacement where the content allows one, and the steps from this view out to everything.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What to type, shown while the field is empty.

props.name: acts_on
props.doc: What the window's find acts on, as the window's reading spells it: `document` (its matches are stepped), `list` (the list narrows), `query` (the app searches itself) or `nothing`. Only a document's matches are stepped; everything else widens on Enter.

props.name: current
props.doc: The match the document stands on, counting from one; `0` with none.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many it found.

props.name: replaces
props.doc: The content's find offers replacing.

props.name: regex
props.doc: And a regular expression.

props.name: hex
props.doc: And hex: the content is bytes.

props.name: match_case
props.doc: The options the find runs under now: whether it matches case.

props.name: match_whole_word
props.doc: And whether it matches whole words only.

props.name: match_regex
props.doc: And whether it reads the query as a regular expression.

props.name: match_hex
props.doc: And whether it reads the query as bytes, in hex.

props.name: app
props.doc: The app's name, for the step that searches all of it ("Search Notes").

props.name: replacing
props.doc: It opened to replace: the replacement takes the keyboard, as Ctrl+H asks.

events.name: changed
events.doc: The query changed as the person typed: what the app's find runs now.

events.name: submit
events.doc: Enter: the field's query is asked again, or, where the find acts on no document, the search widens to the whole app.

events.name: step
events.doc: The person stepped to the next match (`true`) or the one before.

events.name: option
events.doc: The person chose an option: `case`, `whole`, `regex`, `text` or `hex`, to toggle or to set the mode.

events.name: replace
events.doc: The person replaced this match with the text carried.

events.name: replace_all
events.doc: The person replaced every match with the text carried.

events.name: widen
events.doc: The person widened the search: `app` for everything the app holds, `everywhere` for the platform's search over the workspace.

events.name: close
events.doc: The person closed the find, or let go of the field with Escape.

bindings.name: query
bindings.doc: The query, edited in the field.

components.name: FollowFrame
components.doc: The frame round the work while following someone.

props.name: colour
props.doc: The followed person's colour, `rrggbb`; empty while the person follows nobody, and the frame leaves.

semantics.not_in_gallery: it frames the windows a shell lays out, which a gallery has none of

components.name: Fullscreen
components.doc: A view shown filling the audience's screen while it is presented.

props.name: name
props.doc: What it is, for assistive technology and agents.

props.name: showing
props.doc: The view is presented: the window fills the screen until it is not.

props.name: screen
props.doc: Which screen it fills: the audience's, unless said.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: The view it presents.

events.name: exit
events.doc: The person pressed the way out: the view stops presenting what it shows. The control that reports it, "Exit full screen", is drawn while the view is presented; a view leaves it unbound when the system alone ends the presentation.

semantics.label: name
semantics.not_in_gallery: presenting it fills the audience's screen with the view it shows, over the window the gallery is read in, so a gallery page cannot show it without taking that window over

components.name: FunnelChart
components.doc: How many reach each stage of a sequence: the steps of a sign-up, a checkout, a build. Stages narrow as fewer arrive, each with the share of the one before it, or widen as a pyramid; each takes the next colour of the theme's palette.

props.name: stages
props.doc: The stages from the first to the last: `.stage(label: "Visited", value: 1200.0)`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: direction
props.doc: How the stages stand: `funnel` narrowing by how many reach each unless said, `pyramid` widening.

components.name: BarGauge
components.doc: A labelled level as a bar: a disk's use, a quota, a battery.

props.name: value
props.doc: How full it is, from 0 to 1.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it measures: "Storage", "Memory".

props.name: readout
props.doc: The reading over the track's end: "412 GB of 512 GB".

props.name: neutral
props.doc: A share with no status (storage by kind, a quota not yet full): the plain fill, never a status colour.

props.name: warning
props.doc: Where the fill turns warning, from 0 to 1: 0.6 unless said.

props.name: danger
props.doc: Where the fill turns danger, from 0 to 1: 0.85 unless said.

props.name: compact
props.doc: Smaller label and readout, for a dense grid of gauges.

components.name: ProgressRing
components.doc: How full something is, as a ring: a countdown, a download, the one hero reading of a screen (a speed test).

props.name: value
props.doc: How full it is, from 0 to 1.

props.name: readout
props.doc: The readout inside the ring: "42%", "23".

props.name: caption
props.doc: What the readout measures, under it: "seconds", "downloaded".

props.name: size
props.doc: How large it is: `regular` unless said, `small` inline beside text without a readout, `large` for the one hero reading of a screen.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status the fill means: a failed transfer stays danger.

props.name: level
props.doc: A measured level rather than progress: the fill turns warning, then danger, as it fills.

components.name: GraphCanvas
components.doc: Nodes that are views of their own, placed where each says (or in rows when none says), and the connections between them drawn under them: a pipeline, a flow, the parts of a system.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the graph is called: shown over it, as every chart's title is, and its name for assistive technology.

props.name: connections
props.doc: The connections drawn between nodes: `.connection(from: "fetch", to: "build")`, each end a node's id or the test id of a control inside one.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many nodes stand side by side when the nodes give no places: 3 unless said.

props.name: column_width
props.doc: How wide each node is when the nodes give no places, in logical pixels: 200 unless said.

parts.name: nodes
parts.doc: The nodes, in order.

components.name: Heatmap
components.doc: How a value varies across two axes at once: a week by weekday and hour, a year by month and region. Each cell's colour places it between the lowest and the highest value in the theme's ramp; pointing at it reads its value.

props.name: cells
props.doc: Each cell, by the row and column it lies at: `.cell(row: "Monday", column: "9h", value: 12.0)`.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows from top to bottom.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns from left to right.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

components.name: HexGrid
components.doc: Bytes as a dense grid: an offset down the side, hexadecimal pairs and the same bytes as text across, with the cursor, the selection and a search's matches drawn over them.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The rows shown, each its bytes as hexadecimal pairs without spaces (`"00ff2a"`).

props.name: changed
props.doc: For each row, a `"0"` or `"1"` for each byte: whether it differs from what the file holds where it was read.

props.name: total
props.doc: The rows the file has.

props.name: first
props.doc: The row `rows` starts at, counted from 0.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The bytes a row holds: 8 to 64, or 0 for as many as the width holds.

props.name: cursor
props.doc: The byte the cursor is on.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: The other end of the selection: where it is drawn from the cursor.

props.name: column
props.doc: The column the keys edit.

props.name: matches
props.doc: The bytes a search found, each as `"start:end"`, as one of the grid's own bytes.

props.name: at_match
props.doc: The match the cursor is on, by its place in `matches`.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the grid shows, as assistive technology announces it: "bytes.bin, 4096 bytes".

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on a byte runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

events.name: press
events.doc: A byte was pressed: carries its offset, the column pressed, and `"shift"` when Shift held, `["31", "hex", "shift"]`.

events.name: key
events.doc: A key was pressed while the grid had the keyboard: carries it as a person's keyboard names it (`"a"`, `"ArrowLeft"`, `"Ctrl+S"`).

events.name: wheel
events.doc: The wheel or the scroll bar asked to show other rows: carries the rows the first one moves by, down for a positive number.

components.name: Histogram
components.doc: Raw observations as a distribution: how many fell in each bin, so a spread is read at a glance. The bars take the theme's first palette colour and the axis is fitted to the data.

props.name: samples
props.doc: The observations, in any order: `samples: [12.0, 18.0, 15.0, 22.0]`.

props.name: bins
props.doc: How many bins the range is cut into; twelve unless said.

props.name: scale
props.doc: What a bin reads: its `count` unless said, a `probability`, or a `density`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: Icon
components.doc: One glyph from the icon set, in the theme's ink.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The glyph.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large it is: `regular` unless said, `small` beside a caption, `large` beside a title.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: Recede beside its label, in secondary ink.

props.name: accent
props.doc: Take the accent's ink, for the one glyph that marks what is chosen.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status the glyph means, in that status's colour: a passed check, a warning sign.

props.name: description
props.doc: What the glyph means, where it stands without words beside it.

components.name: Image
components.doc: A picture: artwork, a photo, a cover, read from its address.

props.name: src
props.doc: Where the picture's bytes are: a content address (`tilo-blob://<hash>`) or a URL.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture shows, as assistive technology announces it; without one it is decorative.

props.name: fit
props.doc: How it fills its box: `contain`, `cover`, `fill`, or `actual` for its own size.

props.name: input
props.doc: The id whose destination takes its pointer and its keys, when the picture is something a person points and types into — another machine's screen, a stream it runs. Nothing when the picture is just looked at.

components.name: ImageCropEditor
components.doc: A picture with a crop its four corners set (a scanned page, a photo to trim): drag a corner to move it, or an edge's arrow keys, and it reports the crop each time it changes.

props.name: image
props.doc: The picture to crop.

props.name: left
props.doc: The left crop edge, from 0 (the picture's left) to 1.

props.name: top
props.doc: The top crop edge, from 0 (the picture's top) to 1.

props.name: right
props.doc: The right crop edge, to 1 at the picture's right.

props.name: bottom
props.doc: The bottom crop edge, to 1 at the picture's bottom.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The box's shape before the picture is here (its width over its height).

events.name: change
events.doc: The crop changed: carries its edges, left, top, right, bottom, each `0..=1`.

components.name: ImageViewer
components.doc: A picture to look at closely: scroll to zoom at the pointer, drag to pan, and a reset to the whole picture.

props.name: image
props.doc: The picture to show.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture is, as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The box's shape: its width over its height, which it stands at before the picture is here.

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How far the picture is zoomed, 1 being the whole picture: what a view's own zoom controls set. The person's scroll and drag change it too, within the picture, and the view keeps the value it shows.

components.name: InputHint
components.doc: The keys of a shortcut as drawn keycaps, in the person's own keyboard legends.

props.name: keys
props.doc: The keys of the chord, modifiers first: `["Ctrl", "Shift", "P"]`.

components.name: KeyPad
components.doc: The keyboard's keys.

props.name: keys
props.doc: The keys, each with its row and column: the pad lays each row out by the keys' widths, and a key's column is where it stands in its row.

props.name: size
props.doc: How tall a key's rows are, independent of the desktop's density.

props.name: caps
props.doc: Caps Lock is latched: the Shift key stands lit and letters show upper case.

props.name: secret
props.doc: The field is secret: the pad shows no key preview, no alternates and no swipe trail.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press runs now.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the pad shows, as assistive technology announces it: "On-screen keyboard".

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say.

events.name: press
events.doc: A key was pressed: carries its place in `keys` and where the finger was, as fractions of the pad's box, `[index, x, y]`.

events.name: hold
events.doc: A long press chose one of a key's forms: carries its place in `keys` and the form, `[index, form]`.

events.name: swipe
events.doc: A finger crossed the keys and lifted: carries the path in fractions of the pad's box (`x, y, x, y, …`) and the box's width in its heights, so the keys it crossed keep their shape wherever the pad stands.

events.name: caret
events.doc: The person dragged the space bar: carries the caret steps it asks for, left for a negative number.

components.name: Labelled
components.doc: A control a view composed of its own parts (a chooser, a field holding parts of its own), named by the caption the view places beside it: a screen reader and an agent reach it by the words the person reads there. A control that names itself keeps its own name.

props.name: label
props.doc: The caption the view shows beside the control, which names it.

props.name: description
props.doc: A line that explains the control, read after its name.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: The control it names.

components.name: LevelMeter
components.doc: How loud an audio input is right now, as a bar that follows the sound and keeps a falling peak: the component opens the device's meter itself while it runs.

props.name: source
props.doc: The audio device's name, as the sound resource publishes it (the node name).

props.name: output
props.doc: Whether the source is a sink to meter (the volume a speaker plays) rather than a microphone to read.

props.name: running
props.doc: Whether the meter is being read now: it opens only while this is true.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

components.name: Link
components.doc: A hyperlink: primary ink with an underline, opening what it names when pressed.

props.name: url
props.doc: The address it opens (usually also what it says).

props.name: label
props.doc: What it shows, when that is not the address: "The docs".

props.name: item
props.doc: The resource it goes to: activating it opens the resource.

props.name: role
props.doc: What it is set in: `body` unless said.

events.name: activate
events.doc: It was pressed: what pressing it does, instead of opening its address.

components.name: ListRow
components.doc: A row of a list: what an item is, in one line, with the start of its content under it and a quiet fact on its trailing edge.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the item is: its title. A row that names none shows its item's.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: A quiet word before the title, on the same line and in the weaker ink: where an item came from, what it answers.

props.name: item
props.doc: The resource the row shows, which activating the row opens.

props.name: edits
props.doc: The field its title shows, by the address a field bound to it is named by: the item's id and the field's, as an action on it is addressed. An agent's rename there is drawn on the title, as on the field that edits it.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: The line under the title: the start of the item's content, the last message.

props.name: note
props.doc: A line of the row's own under its text: what waits on the item and is not its content, as a proposal about it reads ("Suggested: move this to the end").

props.name: description
props.doc: What assistive technology says after the row's name, beyond the lines the row draws: what the row shows of what it names, for a reader who cannot see it. A row that names one says its secondary line here instead, so nothing is said twice.

props.name: meta
props.doc: When it happened or is due: the first fact of the row's facts column.

props.name: meta_tone
props.doc: The tone the trailing fact reads in, where the item it states has one: a day gone by is overdue.

props.name: value
props.doc: The item's figure among its facts, as a setting shows it.

props.name: badge
props.doc: A short code in the leading column: a method, a kind.

props.name: mark
props.doc: A mark on the row's edge, after every other fact: pinned, starred, an item's priority.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The tone the mark and the row's checkbox ring read in: the item's priority, a theme role rather than a colour.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph in the leading column: what kind of item it is.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether the row is selected in its list.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace the row's own motion plays at: its mark coming and going, and the row arriving, leaving and changing places in its list.

props.name: dense
props.doc: The row stands dense: one quiet line at the caption's size with the small glyph, as tall as that line and its inset, for a reference under content rather than a list of items.

props.name: quiet
props.doc: The row reads as subordinate to the rows around it: its title in the weaker ink, as an outline's quieter branch does.

props.name: disclosure
props.doc: A trailing chevron: activating the row goes on to a page of its own, as a choice that leads to the next step of a flow does.

parts.name: avatar
parts.doc: Who the item is: their face among its facts, between when it is due and how far it has got.

parts.name: trailing
parts.doc: A control on the trailing edge, which moves under the text when the row is narrow.

parts.name: below
parts.doc: What stands under the row's text, in the text's column: a picture of the item, or the line that says why there is none. It is part of the row, read and pressed with it.

events.name: check
events.doc: The checkbox was pressed: what a check is, in the app's words.

events.name: activate
events.doc: The row was activated (a click, Enter, an assistive technology): open what it shows.

bindings.name: checkbox
bindings.doc: A checkbox in the leading column, bound to whether the item is done.

components.name: ControlRow
components.doc: A selectable row of a short list whose items carry their own controls.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether it is the chosen one of its list.

parts.name: children
parts.doc: What the row holds, in order: its thumbnail, its name, and the controls its item has.

events.name: choose
events.doc: It was chosen: a press its controls did not take.

components.name: Magnify
components.doc: An item of a dock that magnifies under the pointer.

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How much larger the item under the pointer stands: `0.6` makes it a little over half again as large at its middle, falling away to its own size a few items off, and `0` leaves it its size.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: What it holds: one item's face.

components.name: Map
components.doc: Places at points on a pannable, zoomable surface, each a view of its own.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the map is, for assistive technology.

props.name: ground
props.doc: Whether it is a desktop: the windows it holds stand on the desktop's ground ([`SurfaceLevel::Ground`](crate::widget::primitives::SurfaceLevel)), not on the content colour of the window the map is in.

props.name: world
props.doc: Whether it is a map of the world: a pin stands centred on the place it names and keeps the size the view gave it on screen at every zoom, and the camera draws back until the whole world fits.

props.name: basemap
props.doc: Where a map of the world's imagery comes from: a tile address with `%z`, `%x` and `%y` standing for the tile's zoom and its column and row (`https://tile.openstreetmap.org/%z/%x/%y.png`). The tiles draw under everything else, scaled with the camera, at the zoom that shows them sharpest; without one the map draws its ground, and a map of the world a faint grid at the places it names. A host serves the pictures (`crate::pictures::set_remote_fetcher`).

props.name: outline
props.doc: A rectangle the view points at, in canvas pixels (`x`, `y`, width, height), drawn as the light outline a drag across the canvas draws: the rectangle the person dragged, kept while they say what fills it.

props.name: hint
props.doc: What the empty map says once, quietly, at the middle of what it shows: what a person does on it ("Click anywhere and say what you want"). Drawn only while it holds no pin, and read to assistive technology as the map's description.

props.name: latitude
props.doc: The latitude the map is centred on, with `longitude`: the place at its middle when the view sets it, so a map of places opens on a place. `None` leaves it a canvas.

props.name: longitude
props.doc: The longitude the map is centred on, with `latitude`.

props.name: zoom
props.doc: The zoom the map opens at, about its centre (`latitude`, `longitude`).

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on its empty surface runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the name does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

parts.name: pins
parts.doc: The pins, in the order the map draws them (the last on top).

parts.name: tracks
parts.doc: The lines drawn across the map under its markers and pins: a route, the way one leg of a journey goes.

parts.name: markers
parts.doc: What stands on the map at a place, drawn as a marker of its own size on screen whatever the zoom: where a search found something, the device's own place. Pointing at one reports it (`marker`); the view opens what it is.

events.name: drop
events.doc: A resource was dragged onto the map and let go: carries the resource the drag carried, as its address, and where it was let go — its canvas x, then its canvas y. The view decides what to do with it; the shell's canvas places it there.

events.name: press
events.doc: The pointer pressed on the map's empty surface — not on a pin — and let go there, having travelled no further than a click: carries the canvas point under the press, its x then its y, kept apart from a drag and a middle drag. What it reports is where the press landed at the camera the map looks with, so the point is right at any pan or zoom; the view decides what stands there (the shell's canvas opens its caret at it).

events.name: frame
events.doc: A left drag across the map's empty surface, let go after travelling: carries the dragged rectangle in canvas pixels, its x, its y, its width and its height. The rectangle is drawn as a light outline while the drag lasts (the theme's focus colour, never a colour of its own), and the view lays what it answers into that rectangle.

events.name: context
events.doc: The pointer's right button pressed on the map: carries the key of the pin pin_places under it — empty text where the press landed on the map's own empty surface — and the canvas point under the pointer, its x then its y. What the view does with it is its own: the shell's canvas opens the pointed place's menu, or the canvas's own for free space (`canvas.md` §1, §6).

events.name: resize
events.doc: A place's trailing edge, bottom edge or corner was dragged and let go: carries the key of the pin it resized and its new size in canvas pixels, its width then its height. Its corner stays where it stood; the view gives the place that size.

events.name: seen
events.doc: The person pointed on the map's free space (a click, a dragged rectangle, a right press): carries the part of the canvas they see as they point, in canvas pixels, its x, its y, its width and its height. It is reported before the pointing itself (`press`, `frame`, `context`), so what answers it can stand in free room where they look (canvas.md §7, "Everything stays in view").

events.name: drawn
events.doc: A hugging pin's view came to a height of its own and the pin is laid out at it: carries the pin's key and its drawn height in canvas pixels. Reported once each time that height changes, never every frame, so a view that reads it as free area on the canvas (`canvas.md` §1, §7) learns what the pin takes without a report a frame.

events.name: rest
events.doc: The camera came to rest where the person left it: carries the place at its middle as its latitude then its longitude, the zoom it shows, and what it shows at its edges as its northern, southern, eastern and western degrees, in that order. Reported once each time a pan, pinch, wheel or key move ends, and never for a move the view itself set, so a view that saves what the person sees knows where they are looking.

events.name: fault
events.doc: The imagery the map shows cannot be loaded: carries how many of the tiles it shows have failed and how many it shows, so the view can say so in words while nothing draws (offline, or the tile server refusing).
