Reported when either number changes, and again with nothing failed once imagery loads.

events.name: at
events.doc: The pointer pressed the map's empty surface and let go there, a click: carries the place under it, its latitude then its longitude, for a map centred on a place.

events.name: marker
events.doc: The pointer pressed a marker and let go there, a click: carries the name the marker was given (`MapMarker`'s `name`), or its key where it has none. The view opens what the marker is; the map reports nothing of its own for that press.

components.name: MediaCard
components.doc: One card: the art (a cover, a thumbnail, a photo) with its title and up to two meta lines under it. A view gives it as a grid's item, on its own, or compact in a band (a pill with the art and the title in one row, `compact`).

props.name: item
props.doc: The resource the card stands for: what a press opens. A card a press runs its own event for stands for nothing.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the card is called, under its art. Without one it is art only (a photo).

props.name: picture
props.doc: Its art: a picture by its address, loaded as it arrives.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon of a kind of thing, on the neutral tile: a podcast, a folder.

props.name: meta
props.doc: One line under the title (an artist, a channel, an author). Give two for two lines.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of its art, `square` unless said.

props.name: compact
props.doc: It stands in a band as a pill rather than as a card: a bar control high, its art at the leading edge and its title beside it. A media session's live view gives this so the shell's bar shows what plays in the bar's own band.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether it is the selected card.

events.name: activate
events.doc: It was pressed: open what it stands for.

components.name: MediaGrid
components.doc: Cards in a grid: a library, an album's covers, a shelf of books, a set of channels.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large each card is: how wide a column holds.

props.name: justified
props.doc: The cards are photos at their own shape: justified rows that span the width, rather than equal columns.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: The cards, in order: given whole, or built by the host as the grid shows them, so a library of ten thousand photographs costs the cards on screen.

events.name: select
events.doc: A range of its cards was taken: carries the cards it stood on, each by the item it shows, in the order they stand. A press with shift takes the cards from the one pressed last to the one pressed now; a press held and dragged over the cards takes the ones it sweeps.

components.name: MediaTransport
components.doc: What is playing and the controls that steer it, as one band: the art and the song, like and lyrics, shuffle, previous, play/pause, next and repeat over the scrubber, the queue and the volume.

props.name: title
props.doc: The song's name, or what the band says with nothing playing.

props.name: subtitle
props.doc: Who it is by, or why it cannot play.

props.name: error
props.doc: The subtitle says why it cannot play: it reads as an error.

props.name: art
props.doc: Its cover: a picture by its address, loaded as it arrives.

props.name: art_name
props.doc: The name the placeholder cover takes its initials and colour from (the album).

props.name: opens
props.doc: What a press on the art opens ("Open album", "Show lyrics"), as it is announced.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Whether it plays.

props.name: idle
props.doc: Nothing can play: every control rests disabled.

props.name: position
props.doc: Where it is, in seconds.

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long it is, in seconds.

props.name: volume
props.doc: The volume, `0..=1`; zero is muted.

props.name: shuffle
props.doc: Whether shuffle is on. Without it there is no shuffle control.

props.name: repeat
props.doc: What repeat repeats. Without it there is no repeat control.

props.name: liked
props.doc: Whether what plays is liked. Without it there is no like control.

props.name: lyrics
props.doc: Whether the lyrics show. Without it there is no lyrics control.

props.name: queue
props.doc: Whether the queue shows. Without it there is no queue control.

props.name: source
props.doc: Where the sound plays from: a file's address or a stream's URL the engine fetches. With one the band plays it and its scrubber follows the sound; without one it only shows what the view declares.

events.name: act_play_pause
events.doc: The play/pause control was pressed.

events.name: act_previous
events.doc: The previous control was pressed.

events.name: act_next
events.doc: The next control was pressed.

events.name: act_shuffle
events.doc: Shuffle was toggled.

events.name: act_repeat
events.doc: Repeat was toggled.

events.name: act_like
events.doc: What plays was liked or unliked.

events.name: act_mute
events.doc: The band was muted or unmuted.

events.name: act_seek
events.doc: The band was moved to a place in the song: carries `0..=1`.

events.name: act_volume
events.doc: The volume was set: carries `0..=1`.

events.name: act_lyrics
events.doc: The lyrics were asked for.

events.name: act_queue
events.doc: The queue was asked for.

events.name: ended
events.doc: What played reached its end: the app moves on to what comes next.

events.name: progress
events.doc: Where playback got to while it played, as a share of its length (`0..=1`): reported on the first five-second step, then once per step, and once more when it stops or ends, so a view remembers the place a song was left at even when nobody moved the playhead.

events.name: length
events.doc: How long the sound runs, in seconds, once the engine has read it: what a song opened from a file is long, which its name does not say.

events.name: fail
events.doc: The engine could not play the source: carries what it said, and where in the song it stopped, in seconds. A stream a source serves only partway through stops here, and the app asks the source for a fresh address and continues from that place.

components.name: Money
components.doc: An amount of money in millionths of the currency (`$5`, `$0.42`, `$1,250`), as the toolkit writes money: whole amounts without cents, fractional ones with two places, grouped and marked by the person's number style.

props.name: micros
props.doc: The amount, in millionths of the currency.

props.name: role
props.doc: What the text is, which sets its size and weight: `body` unless said.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: Beside the content it is about, in secondary ink: what a turn cost, under its answer.

components.name: NavList
components.doc: A sidebar of places whose choice is reported to the app: choosing one shows it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading over the places.

props.name: selected
props.doc: The key of the place shown now.

props.name: rail
props.doc: A compact rail of icons that fits beside the content at every width.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: The places, in order, and sections of them under a heading.

events.name: select
events.doc: A place was chosen: its key is the value.

events.name: reorder
events.doc: A place was dropped on another: carries the place's key and the key it was dropped on, in that order. The app moves its own list; the list keeps no order of its own.

components.name: NavShell
components.doc: A window's shell: a sidebar of places, an overview list, the content and an inspector side by side while they fit, and one at a time with Back when they do not.

props.name: content_kind
props.doc: What the content is, which sets the narrowest it still works at: `page` unless said.

props.name: title
props.doc: The content's title, in its header.

props.name: content_key
props.doc: What the content shows, as the app names it (the pane in front, the place opened): when it changes, what the content shows fades in where the one before it stood, on the theme's cross-fade. Nothing when the content is not a thing that changes.

props.name: count
props.doc: How many things the content lists, beside its title.

props.name: overview_title
props.doc: The overview column's title.

props.name: overview_count
props.doc: How many things the overview lists, beside its title.

props.name: sidebar_title
props.doc: The sidebar's title: what the places are of, the app's root.

props.name: can_go_back
props.doc: Whether the content's Back goes back now (a drill-down the app keeps).

props.name: page
props.doc: The view was opened as a page of its own (`open(r, view: v)`, a search hit's view): the window places it over what it showed, a list beside it or not, and gives it Back.

props.name: nothing_listed
props.doc: Nothing at all to list: what `content` gives is the window's empty state, in place of the overview, the content and the inspector.

props.name: sidebar_collapse
props.doc: How the sidebar stands in a window too narrow to dock it: the shell's own rule (`auto`), a drawer over the content (`drawer`), or a screen of the push stack (`screen`).

props.name: inspector_collapse
props.doc: How the inspector stands in a window too narrow to dock it: a sheet up from the window's foot (`sheet`, the default) or a drawer in from its trailing edge (`drawer`).

props.name: sidebar_open
props.doc: Whether the view asks for the sidebar open (`true`) or closed (`false`). Applied when it changes; the person's own toggle stands until the view asks for another state.

props.name: inspector_open
props.doc: Whether the view asks for the inspector open or closed. Applied when it changes; the person's own toggle stands until the view asks for another state.

parts.name: sidebar_actions
parts.doc: The sidebar's controls in its header: the action that makes what it lists (a "+"), and where a person's new thing goes.

parts.name: sidebar
parts.doc: The places of the app: a navigation list.

parts.name: overview
parts.doc: The list the content is chosen from.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What the window is for.

parts.name: inspector
parts.doc: Details of what the content shows, beside it.

parts.name: actions
parts.doc: The content's actions, in its header.

parts.name: band
parts.doc: The band across the window's foot: what plays, and the controls that steer it, under every column. An app that shows a player puts it here, as the native shell did.

parts.name: overview_actions
parts.doc: The overview's actions, in its header: what the list's owner offers.

events.name: back
events.doc: The content's Back was pressed.

events.name: search
events.doc: The text the window's search holds, narrowing what the frame lists as a chosen place does; empty while the search is closed.

events.name: drop
events.doc: Files were dropped on the window, anywhere no component of its own took them: each as a `File` — its name, its media type, its size and where its bytes are — kept by the window. What an app takes a dropped document with, wherever on it the person lets go.

state.name: pane
state.doc: The column in front of a narrow window.

components.name: NumberInput
components.doc: A number with a step either side (a page size, a margin, a count), set by typing, its steppers and the arrow keys within its range.

props.name: label
props.doc: The number's spoken name, for a field with no label beside it.

props.name: min
props.doc: The smallest it may be.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest it may be.

props.name: step
props.doc: How much one press of a stepper adds; 1 unless said.

props.name: precision
props.doc: Decimal places it shows: 0 unless said, for a whole number.

props.name: suffix
props.doc: A unit after the number, shown and not typed: "px", "%".

props.name: compact
props.doc: Smaller, for a toolbar: bare steppers, no field frame.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be changed now.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The value, and where a change of it goes.

components.name: PagePreview
components.doc: A page's shape in a print queue, a scan or a picker: a sheet with the lines a page has and "Page n of m" under it, showing the shape and never the content.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the page is: its file's name, for assistive technology.

props.name: page
props.doc: Which page this is, counted from 1 (clamped into the count).

props.name: page_count
props.doc: How many pages the document has.

components.name: PageSidebar
components.doc: A rail of numbered page thumbnails down a document's side; unless read-only, pages are dragged, copied, moved and added.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: A page's height over its width (`1.414` for A4, `792/612` for US Letter).

props.name: count
props.doc: How many pages the document has.

props.name: current
props.doc: Which page is open, counted from 0.

props.name: header
props.doc: The rail's title above the thumbnails; "Pages" in the window's language when unset.

props.name: add
props.doc: The label of the button that adds a page at the foot ("Import…"); without it there is no add button.

props.name: panel
props.doc: The rail paints the document's whole side panel; without it it paints only the thumbnails, on the host's background.

props.name: pictures
props.doc: Each page's picture, by address, in page order: what its thumbnail shows. A page with no address, or one whose picture is still loading, keeps its placeholder tile.

events.name: select
events.doc: A page was chosen: its index, counted from 0, is the value.

events.name: reorder
events.doc: A page was moved: its old index, then its place among the others.

events.name: duplicate
events.doc: A page was to be copied: its index is the value.

events.name: delete
events.doc: A page was to be removed: its index is the value.

events.name: add_page
events.doc: A page was to be added.

components.name: PageSlide
components.doc: One page of a stack that a view shows in place, the replaced page leaving as it swaps: a panel opening a deeper page, and Back sliding it away.

props.name: level
props.doc: How deep the page is: 0 the first page, 1 the page it opens.

parts.name: page
parts.doc: The page it shows.

components.name: PaintSurface
components.doc: A surface a person paints on: the artwork beneath, the stroke under the hand previewed over it.

props.name: picture
props.doc: The artwork as it stands, its layers composited: the picture under the paint.

props.name: width
props.doc: The artwork's width in its own units.

props.name: height
props.doc: The artwork's height in its own units.

props.name: brush
props.doc: The brush that lays a stroke; the round ink brush when none is named.

props.name: size
props.doc: The brush's width in artwork units.

props.name: colour
props.doc: The colour a stroke lays, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`; ink when none is named.

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How far the view is zoomed in; 1 fits the artwork in the surface.

props.name: pan
props.doc: The artwork unit at the surface's top left: where the view looks.

props.name: overlay
props.doc: A picture laid over the artwork, such as a comparison's changed region.

props.name: overlay_rect
props.doc: The frame the overlay fills, `[x, y, width, height]` in artwork units; the whole artwork when absent.

props.name: overlay_opacity
props.doc: How strongly the overlay shows over the artwork, 0 to 1 (default 1).

props.name: label
props.doc: What it shows, as assistive technology announces it.

events.name: stroke_start
events.doc: A stroke began, at `[x, y, pressure]` in the artwork's units.

events.name: stroke
events.doc: A stroke went on, at `[x, y, pressure]` in the artwork's units.

events.name: stroke_end
events.doc: A stroke ended where the hand lifted, at `[x, y, pressure]`.

events.name: hover
events.doc: The pointer moved over the surface, at `[x, y]` in the artwork's units.

events.name: wheel
events.doc: The wheel turned over the surface: `[across, down]` in logical pixels.

events.name: pinch
events.doc: A pinch over the surface: the scale factor the fingers ask for, 1 for none.

events.name: panned
events.doc: A middle-button drag panned the view by `[dx, dy]` artwork units.

components.name: PeerPointers
components.doc: Other people's pointers over the window of a place.

props.name: place
props.doc: The place whose window they are over: the tab id the shell model gives the window.

parts.name: pointers
parts.doc: The pointers, in the order the roster lists their people.

semantics.not_in_gallery: its pointers stand over a window a gallery has none of

components.name: PersonField
components.doc: A form's person, shown as an avatar and name and picked from the workspace's members and agents; "Me" is the person the view is shown to, "No one" clears it.

props.name: people
props.doc: The people offered after "Me" and "No one": the workspace's members and agents.

props.name: me
props.doc: The person the view is shown to: the list's "Me".

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The binding a pick writes: the person picked, empty for nobody.

components.name: PictureChoice
components.doc: A choice among pictures whose meaning is visual (a text size, a pointer size, a colour filter), each tile showing its picture over its name, the chosen one edged.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Which tile is chosen, counted from 0: none until a person chooses one.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be chosen from now.

parts.name: options
parts.doc: The tiles, in order.

events.name: change
events.doc: A tile was chosen: its index, counted from 0, is the value.

components.name: PieChart
components.doc: The parts of one whole as the slices of a pie: how a total divides. Each slice takes the next colour of the theme's palette and is named in a legend with its share.

props.name: slices
props.doc: The parts, in order: `.slice(label: "Open", value: 12.0)`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: ring
props.doc: A ring rather than a full pie, with `total` read at its centre.

props.name: total
props.doc: What a ring reads at its centre: the whole, as it reads ("128 issues").

props.name: unit
props.doc: What a part's value counts, written after it where a person pointing at it reads it ("GB", "h").

components.name: PolarAreaChart
components.doc: A cycle's magnitudes around a circle: months of the year, hours of the day, weekdays. Every direction takes the same angle and its length carries the value, so seasonal shape is read at a glance; each takes the next colour of the theme's palette.

props.name: areas
props.doc: The directions in order, clockwise from the top: `.area(label: "January", value: 12.0)`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: BarChip
components.doc: A bar control for people: their faces, a label and a press, with faces opening who is here and an invite opening the host's invite flow.

props.name: name
props.doc: The chip's name for assistive technology, and its tooltip when it shows only a glyph.

props.name: label
props.doc: The words beside the faces: "Editing", "Invite".

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the faces: a watch, an invitation.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: A trailing glyph: the chevron of a chip that opens a panel.

props.name: who
props.doc: Who it shows, in order: their faces, then a count for everyone past them.

props.name: open
props.doc: The chip's panel is open: the chip is lifted as a whole.

props.name: focused
props.doc: Keyboard focus; the ring shows only while focus is visible.

props.name: label_width
props.doc: The most the label may grow to before it elides.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A person whose presence colour washes the chip's body: who the state it says is about.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be pressed now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the name does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside the name, and shown on hover.

events.name: press
events.doc: A press: the chip's action.

components.name: DisclosureRow
components.doc: A row whose body opens under it (a device's details, a run's log, a setting's options), its chevron turning as the rows below move down; a press, Enter or Space opens and closes it.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the row is, on its first line.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: A line under the title, in secondary ink.

props.name: side
props.doc: A quiet line at the far end of the title's line: who did it and when.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the title: the kind of thing it is.

props.name: who
props.doc: A person before the title, as an avatar: who did the work the row shows.

props.name: signal
props.doc: How strong a radio network's signal is, before the title, for a row that is a network.

props.name: expanded
props.doc: Whether the row is open; unless given the row keeps it.

props.name: dense
props.doc: One quiet line among content rather than a row of a list: the caption's size and ink, as tall as that line (an answer's steps, folded under it).

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace the body unfolds at, and a view's open or close: the theme's unless said.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: What opens under the row, in order.

parts.name: trailing
parts.doc: One control on the row's trailing edge, before the chevron (a device's Connect): it acts without opening the row.

events.name: toggle
events.doc: The row was opened or closed: whether it is open now is the value.

components.name: Facts
components.doc: Facts in one row, each an optional glyph and its text, spaced apart with no separator ("12 files", "3 MB", "Edited today"); when the row is too narrow the least important give way first.

parts.name: facts
parts.doc: The facts, in order.

components.name: KeyHints
components.doc: Shortcuts and what they do, side by side, each hint the drawn keycaps of a chord and its label ("Enter Save") in the person's keyboard legends.

parts.name: hints
parts.doc: The hints, in order.

components.name: ModalDialog
components.doc: A question over the window: a dimmed page, a sheet with a title, the content and up to three answers; Escape or the scrim closes it, and Enter fires the main answer, or the safe one when it destroys something.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the question is, as its title (name the action: "Delete 3 notes?").

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the title naming what asks.

props.name: description
props.doc: What assistive technology says after the title.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether it is open; a closed dialog paints nothing and takes no input.

props.name: primary
props.doc: The main answer's label ("Delete"): the inverted button, and what Enter fires.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: The other answer's label, usually Cancel. Escape fires it.

props.name: tertiary
props.doc: A third answer's label, set apart ("Don't save"); Enter never fires it.

props.name: destructive
props.doc: The main answer destroys something: it is a destructive button, and Enter is the safe answer instead.

props.name: primary_enabled
props.doc: The main answer cannot be taken yet, so it is disabled.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: The view's content, inside the sheet.

events.name: act_primary
events.doc: The main answer was taken.

events.name: act_secondary
events.doc: The other answer was taken.

events.name: act_tertiary
events.doc: The third answer was taken.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: It was closed (Escape, the scrim, or Cancel): a dialog with this closes as it is.

components.name: FloatingPanel
components.doc: A floating panel with a header part, a body and a footer part, which a view rarely places itself: a menu is a `Popover` and a question a `ModalDialog`.

props.name: width
props.doc: A fixed width, in logical pixels (a utility panel).

props.name: fill_height
props.doc: Take the height it is offered rather than the height of its content: a panel a surface measured a room for, whose body scrolls inside it when it holds more.

props.name: fill
props.doc: Take the width it is offered rather than the width of its content: a card that spans a narrow display.

props.name: label
props.doc: What assistive technology calls it; a panel that names none adds no node of its own.

props.name: description
props.doc: What assistive technology says after its name.

props.name: modal
props.doc: It holds the screen while it shows: what it covers is dimmed, fading with the panel, and it reads as a modal dialog.

props.name: slide
props.doc: It arrives from its trailing edge on the panel slide, as a banner rises in the corner.

props.name: x
props.doc: Where it stands, from the top-leading corner of what holds it, in logical pixels: its left edge. With `y`, the panel stands there rather than where its siblings put it.

props.name: y
props.doc: Its top edge, from the top of what holds it, in logical pixels.

props.name: edge
props.doc: The edge of what holds it it is kept at (`left`, `right`, `bottom`, `bottom_left` or `bottom_right`), rather than a place: it stands in that edge's slot, the toolkit's margin in from it, and `x` and `y` say nothing.

props.name: shown
props.doc: Whether it is up; absent, it is. A panel that is not comes in when it is, and goes when it is no more, on the shared motion and where it stands; while it is not up it takes no input and names nothing.

parts.name: body
parts.doc: The panel's body.

parts.name: header
parts.doc: Its header, above the body; a field there renders embedded.

parts.name: footer
parts.doc: Its footer, under the body.

events.name: moved
events.doc: The person dragged it by its header and let it go: carries where it settled, its left and top edge from the top-leading corner of what holds it, onto an edge it was let go near and inside what holds it. A panel with this moves when its header is dragged.

events.name: resized
events.doc: The person drew its trailing edge out or in and let it go: carries the width it rests at, in logical pixels. A panel with this resizes when that edge is dragged, following it.

events.name: docked
events.doc: The person dragged a panel kept at an edge by its header and let it go: carries the edge nearest where they let it go, by its name. A panel with this moves when its header is dragged; a press that never moves past the slop, a pointer leaving and Escape move nothing.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: A press landed off the panel, on nothing of its own: a panel with this is dismissed by it.

components.name: Popover
components.doc: A menu or a small form anchored beside its control, with the view's content inside it.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its accessible name (a menu says what it chooses: "Refresh interval").

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether it is open.

props.name: side
props.doc: The side of its anchor it prefers: `below` unless said.

props.name: at
props.doc: The point it stands at, `[x, y]` from the top-left of where it is declared: where a press raised it (a question an action asks first). Its primary button stands under that point, so pressing again at the same spot takes it.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: Its content.

events.name: dismiss
events.doc: It was closed (Escape, or a press outside it): a popover with this closes as it is.

components.name: PopoverButton
components.doc: A button that opens a popover anchored to itself (a filter's options, a share sheet); a second press, Escape or a press outside closes it.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the button is called, as it is announced.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the label, or instead of it when `icon_only`.

props.name: icon_only
props.doc: The glyph alone, with the label as its tooltip and accessible name.

props.name: side
props.doc: The side of the button it opens on: `below` unless said.

props.name: trailing
props.doc: Whether it opens at the button's trailing edge, not its leading edge.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: The popover's content.

components.name: TextStack
components.doc: A title over a secondary line and an optional third (a file's name over its folder, a person over their role), each one line cut short with an ellipsis.

props.name: title
props.doc: The first line, in the body's medium weight.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: The line under the title, in secondary ink.

props.name: tertiary
props.doc: A third line, in tertiary ink.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status the secondary line means, in its colour: "Failed" in danger.

props.name: dense
props.doc: A dense row's or a bar's stack: a smaller title.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.doc: How far something is (a transfer, an import, a sync): without a value a segment slides across the track with no known end, and a measured level (a disk, a quota) turns warning then danger as it fills.

props.name: value
props.doc: The share done, from 0 to 1; without it the bar has no known end.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is under way ("Uploading"), shown over the track; a named bar announces its progress without taking focus.

props.name: accessible_name
props.doc: How assistive technology names it where no label shows: a step track under a heading that already says the step is named by the whole stage ("Identity setup, step 2 of 4: Protect") without repeating it over the track. A shown label names it otherwise.

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status the fill means: a failed transfer stays danger.

props.name: level
props.doc: A measured level instead of progress: the fill turns warning, then danger, as it fills.

props.name: warning
props.doc: Where a level turns warning, from 0 to 1: 0.6 unless said.

props.name: danger
props.doc: Where a level turns danger, from 0 to 1: 0.85 unless said.

components.name: PropertyList
components.doc: Facts about one thing, a label beside each value: a contact's details, a file's.

props.name: striped
props.doc: Shade every other row, for a long list read across.

parts.name: properties
parts.doc: The facts, in order.

components.name: QrCode
components.doc: A QR code of a payload for a phone's camera to read (a pairing handshake, an invite); a private payload is left out of screenshots and screens and never spoken.

props.name: payload
props.doc: What the code carries, as the scanner reads it.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What scanning it means, as assistive technology announces it: "QR code" unless said.

props.name: secret
props.doc: The payload is private pairing material: leave the code out of screenshots and recordings, and never speak it.

components.name: RadarChart
components.doc: Several measures of the same things on axes around a circle, each axis with its own scale: a thing's shape reads at a glance, and several things compare by overlay. Each series takes the next colour of the theme's palette and is named in a legend.

props.name: axes
props.doc: The axes in order, around the circle from the top: `.axis(label: "Speed", max: 100.0)`.

props.name: series
props.doc: Each thing read across the axes: `.series(values: [12.0, 8.0], label: "This week")`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.doc: A short list of choices, exactly one of which is made, each a radio beside its words: for a choice a person reads before making (how a report is sent, who may open a page). A few short choices that switch a setting at once are a `ToggleGroup`; many are a `Dropdown`. The group is one stop of the keyboard's order, and the arrow keys move the choice along it.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Which choice is made, counted from 0: none until the person makes one.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name: what the choices are of.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether any of it can be chosen now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why none of it can be chosen, while none can: its tooltip, and what assistive technology reads.

parts.name: options
parts.doc: The choices, in order.

events.name: change
events.doc: A choice was made: carries its index, counted from 0.

components.name: RangeChart
components.doc: What takes a span of something, one row each: when things happen on a timeline, a plan's rows and how far each has come, the hours a room is booked, or the moments something happened. Each row is named before its bar and read out with its interval.

props.name: ranges
props.doc: The rows, top to bottom: `.range(label: "Design review", start: 2.0, end: 5.0, progress: 0.6)`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, at its head and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: kind
props.doc: What it shows: `timeline` spans unless said, a `plan` whose rows fill to their progress, `intervals` between numbers, or `milestones` at points.

props.name: axis
props.doc: What the axis under the rows measures ("October", "Hour").

props.name: unit
props.doc: What an axis value counts, written after it ("min", "°C").

components.name: Time
components.doc: A moment as how long ago or how far ahead it was (`2 min ago`, `Yesterday`, `in 3 min`) in the person's language and time zone, changing only when its text does.

props.name: at
props.doc: The moment.

props.name: role
props.doc: What the text is, which sets its size and weight: `body` unless said.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: Beside the content it is about, in secondary ink: when a change was made.

props.name: past
props.doc: The moment has happened, as a received message or a logged entry: one the reader's clock has not reached reads `just now`, never ahead.

props.name: clock
props.doc: Show the time of day in the person's zone (`5:16 AM`), as a transcript shows when a message was sent; the day it falls on is the transcript's divider, never this line.

components.name: Rule
components.doc: A horizontal rule of a size the view gives it, its ends ticked: what a view measures (a map's scale bar) rather than a divider that fills its row.

props.name: length
props.doc: How long it draws, in logical pixels. Without one it fills the row it stands in.

props.name: ticks
props.doc: A tick stands at each end, as a measurement's ends do.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it is, for assistive technology.

components.name: SankeyChart
components.doc: Where a quantity moves between stages: visits that become trials, hours that become work, money that becomes cost. Each stage is a column of nodes as tall as what passes through them, each link a ribbon as thick as its share, its nodes and links named where they fit; a person pointing at one reads what it carries.

props.name: nodes
props.doc: The stages and sources, in order: `.node(id: "visits", label: "Visits")`. Its stage is the longest chain of links that leads to it.

props.name: links
props.doc: What moves between them: `.link(from: "visits", to: "signup", value: 72.0)`, `from` and `to` naming nodes by their ids.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, over it and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: ScreenMirror
components.doc: Someone's screen as a picture of where they are.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the picture says to a person who cannot see it: whose screen it is.

props.name: screen_width
props.doc: Their screen's width, logical pixels: with `screen_height`, the shape the picture keeps.

props.name: screen_height
props.doc: Their screen's height, logical pixels.

props.name: colour
props.doc: Their colour, `rrggbb`: the ring of the window they work in.

props.name: height
props.doc: How tall the picture stands, logical pixels; the screen keeps its shape inside it.

props.name: followed
props.doc: The person looking follows them: their colour runs the picture's whole height, saying whose view this is.

parts.name: windows
parts.doc: Their windows, in the order they paint.

components.name: Scroll
components.doc: A body that scrolls under its column's fixed header, showing the part of the content the column fits.

props.name: follow_end
props.doc: Open at the end of the content and stay there while it grows, unless the person scrolled away: a transcript, whose newest line is last.

props.name: across
props.doc: Scroll sideways instead: a row wider than its column, such as a board's lists.

props.name: both
props.doc: Scroll both ways, for a 2D surface wider and taller than its column (a board of strips); takes precedence over `across`.

props.name: shows_bar
props.doc: Show the bar for as long as the content overflows, not only while it is scrolled: a card held to a height whose words go on below it, so the person sees there is more.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the region holds, for assistive technology: Tab stops on a region whose content overflows and announces it ("Identity setup, step 2 of 4: Protect").

props.name: reveals_focus
props.doc: Scroll a control that takes the keyboard into view: a form held to a card's height, whose next field Tab reaches below the fold. Scrolling away from the same control stays put.

props.name: keep
props.doc: Keep the descendant that names itself this (`Widget::kept_in_view`) in view when the one that is named changes: the front strip of a row a person pans, brought into view as they move between windows.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: What scrolls.

components.name: Section
components.doc: A group of related content under an optional title (a list's rows, fields, a figure); a collapsible one opens and closes under its title.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the group is about.

props.name: collapsible
props.doc: Whether its title opens and closes it.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace the content arrives and leaves at, and its title's reveal: the theme's unless said.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: The content, in order.

events.name: toggle
events.doc: A collapsible section opened or closed: whether it is open now is the value.

state.name: expanded
state.doc: Whether a collapsible section shows what it holds.

components.name: ObjectHeader
components.doc: The head of a detail view: an avatar or glyph, the thing's name and one caption line under it ("Ada Lovelace" over "ada@example.org").

props.name: title
props.doc: The thing's name.

props.name: caption
props.doc: One line under the name: an address, a URL, a kind.

props.name: who
props.doc: A person before the name, as their avatar.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A glyph before the name: the kind of thing it is.

props.name: square
props.doc: The avatar is square: an account or a site, not a person.

components.name: StatusLine
components.doc: A status as a sentence: a dot in the status's colour beside a caption ("Engine running", "3 containers stopped"), for a list's footer or a detail's state; it is never pressed.

props.name: text
props.doc: The sentence: "Synced 2 minutes ago".

props.name: status
props.doc: What state it says: `active` (running, connected, healthy) unless said, `warning` (needs attention soon), `error` (failed or offline unexpectedly), `idle` (present but inactive).

props.name: who
props.doc: A person whose presence it says, in their colour, instead of a status.

components.name: Sheet
components.doc: A sheet drawn as a grid: its column and row headers, its cells as they show, the cells the person chose, the cells a search found and a comment's mark in the corner.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the sheet is, for assistive technology.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many columns it shows.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many rows it shows.

props.name: column_width
props.doc: A column's width in pixels where the person did not size it.

props.name: row_height
props.doc: A row's height in pixels where the person did not size it.

props.name: sizes
props.doc: The columns and rows the person sized.

props.name: cells
props.doc: The cells that show anything; an empty cell takes no room here.

props.name: selection
props.doc: The cells chosen, as `A1` or `A1:B2`.

props.name: found
props.doc: The cells the window's search found.

props.name: commented
props.doc: The cells a comment is on.

props.name: answered
props.doc: The cells a resolved comment is on.

props.name: peers
props.doc: Who else is in the sheet, where they are.

props.name: editable
props.doc: It takes edits; read-only when not.

events.name: select
events.doc: The cells chosen changed: carries them, as `A1` or `A1:B2`.

events.name: edit
events.doc: Cells were written: carries pairs of reference and input, in order; an empty input clears its cell.

events.name: resized_column
events.doc: A column was resized: carries its letter and its new width in pixels.

events.name: resized_row
events.doc: A row was resized: carries its number and its new height in pixels.

events.name: fill
events.doc: The fill handle was dragged: carries the cells it copies from and the cells it fills.

events.name: copy
events.doc: The chosen cells were asked to be copied: carries them as a table, a line per row and a tab between columns. The app's action writes it to the person's clipboard.

events.name: cut
events.doc: The chosen cells were asked to be cut: carries them as `copy` does, and the app copies them and clears the cells.

events.name: paste
events.doc: The person asked to paste: the app reads the person's clipboard and writes the cells from the selection's top left.

components.name: ShortcutRecorder
components.doc: A keyboard shortcut as keycaps that are the control: pressing them records a new chord, with a reset while it differs from the default.

props.name: default
props.doc: The chord it started as, which its reset puts back.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name: the command the shortcut runs.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The chord, as its text ("Ctrl+Shift+K"), and where a recorded one goes.

components.name: InState
components.doc: A control as it looks in one state of interaction (hovered, pressed, focused), held still and taking no input: the states of a button or a field side by side, as a style guide or a page of documentation shows them. Disabled, checked, chosen and invalid are the control's own props; this shows what only a pointer or the keyboard otherwise gives it. Assistive technology skips it: the control it shows is a picture of one, not one to use.

props.name: state
props.doc: The state its content is shown in.

parts.name: content
parts.doc: The control shown.

components.name: SignalMeter
components.doc: How strong a radio signal is (a Wi-Fi network, a mobile network), as four bars one icon square in size, naming itself by its level: "Strong signal".

props.name: level
props.doc: How strong the signal is: `unknown` fills no bar.

components.name: Skeleton
components.doc: The shape of content still on its way, drawn where it will be and at its size so nothing moves when it arrives; it never shimmers and says "Loading" to assistive technology.

props.name: shape
props.doc: What it previews: `text` unless said.

props.name: lines
props.doc: How many lines: of text (3 unless said), or under a row's title (none unless said).

props.name: leading
props.doc: What leads a row: a mark, an avatar or a tile.

props.name: aspect
props.doc: The shape of a media card's art: `square` unless said.

props.name: height
props.doc: A block's height in logical pixels.

components.name: Slider
components.doc: A value along a track (a level, a volume, a share), set by dragging the knob or pressing the track and stepped by the arrow keys, finely with Shift.

props.name: label
props.doc: The value's spoken name, for a slider with no label beside it: "Volume".

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest value, 0 unless said.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest value, 1 unless said.

props.name: step
props.doc: Values snap to multiples of this from the minimum; the arrow keys move one step.

props.name: stops
props.doc: The values it stops at, marked along the track: a drag lands on the nearest, the arrow keys go from one to the next (the versions along a history).

props.name: shows_value
props.doc: Show the value in words beside the track: "72%".

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be moved now.

events.name: change
events.doc: The person moved it: the value it is at now is the value.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The value, and where a change of it goes.

components.name: Slideshow
components.doc: A picture shown large in the window for its time, then the next asked for: a presentation a view opens, with the slide it shows kept by the view.

props.name: image
props.doc: The picture on screen now.

props.name: alt
props.doc: What the picture is, as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: seconds
props.doc: How long it stays before the next is asked for, in seconds.

events.name: next
events.doc: The picture has been shown its time: the view asks for the next.

components.name: Spinner
components.doc: Something under way whose length is not known, four dots turning and holding still under reduced motion; a progress bar or ring says how far when the share is known.

props.name: label
props.doc: What is under way ("Loading messages"), as assistive technology names it.

props.name: beside
props.doc: Size it to one line of this text, for a spinner beside a status line; alone at its full size unless said.

components.name: Stage
components.doc: A page of a fixed size, with what stands on it placed in the page's own coordinates.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the stage is, for assistive technology.

props.name: canvas
props.doc: The page's own size, its width then its height (a slide is 1280, 720).

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How many logical pixels one page coordinate takes, as the person chose it: the page is fitted to the stage's box, whole and centred, unless said. The stage's wheel, pinch and keys report the zoom they took (`zoomed`), so a view that keeps it here finds the zoom where the person left it after a rebuild.

props.name: pan
props.doc: How far the page is moved from centred, in logical pixels, its x then its y: the stage keeps it within the travel the page's edges allow and reports the pan it took (`panned`).

props.name: background
props.doc: The colour the page itself is painted in, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`; none leaves it clear.

props.name: chosen
props.doc: The place the view chose, by its item or key: drawn with its frame, so the person sees what they are working on.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on the page runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the name does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

props.name: still
props.doc: The stage stands the page where the view puts it and takes nothing of its own: the wheel and a pinch do not zoom it, no pan moves it, the keys that walk and move its places do not reach it, and a dragged place does not line up with the page's margins. A stage laid over a page another view draws sets this, so the page under it keeps its own zoom and its own keys and its places move only where the hand puts them.

props.name: transition
props.doc: How the stage plays another page swapped for the one it shows: `.cross_fade` keeps the page that was shown laid out while it fades out and fades the new one in over it, for a stage that presents one page at a time. A change of the same page (a moved place, a zoom) is reconciled in place and never swaps.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace a page swap plays at: `.standard` (the theme's, and what the stage does anyway), `.brisk`, `.calm`, or `.still`, whose swaps land at once.

parts.name: pins
parts.doc: What stands on the page, back to front.

events.name: press
events.doc: The person pressed the page's own empty surface and let go there, travelling no further than a click: carries the page point, its x then its y.

events.name: select
events.doc: The person pressed a place: carries what it stands for and the page point.

events.name: moved
events.doc: The person dragged a place to a new place on the page: carries what it stands for and its new page point. Reported as the hand moves, as one gesture, so everyone looking sees it move and one undo takes the whole move back.

events.name: resized
events.doc: The person dragged a place's trailing edge, bottom edge or corner: carries what it stands for and its new width and height in page coordinates. Its top-leading corner stays.

events.name: context
events.doc: The person pressed a place with the right button: carries what it stands for and the page point.

events.name: zoomed
events.doc: The person zoomed the page, by a wheel with the command modifier, a pinch or a key: carries the zoom they chose, in logical pixels a page coordinate, or 0 for the page fitted whole. A view that keeps it and gives it back as `zoom` finds the zoom where the person left it after a rebuild.

events.name: panned
events.doc: The person moved the page: carries its new pan, its x then its y in window pixels. A view that keeps it and gives it back as `pan` finds the page where the person left it.

events.name: open
events.doc: The person pressed Enter on the chosen place: carries what it stands for. The view opens it — a text box takes the typing.

events.name: delete
events.doc: The person pressed Delete on the chosen place: carries what it stands for. The view removes it.

components.name: StatGroup
components.doc: Stat tiles that reflow by width: one row when they fit, then half per row (2 by 2 for four), then one per row; separated by space, never boxed.

parts.name: tiles
parts.doc: The tiles, in order.

components.name: StatTile
components.doc: One number and what it measures (a dashboard's reading, a backup's size), read top to bottom as a label, the value with its unit, a note, its trend and a sparkline; a tile that opens a detail is pressed.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the number measures, in sentence case: "Active users".

props.name: value
props.doc: The number, as it reads: "1,284", "99.9".

props.name: unit
props.doc: Its unit, after the value: "GB", "ms".

props.name: note
props.doc: A neutral qualifier read with the value: "of 2 TB", "estimated".

props.name: change
props.doc: How it changed, beside an arrow of its trend: "12% this week".

props.name: trend
props.doc: Which way it moved: `up` unless said, when it has a change; its tone, not the arrow, says whether that is good.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The state of what it measures, as a ticker down its leading edge: a failed backup is danger, a healthy tunnel success.

props.name: hero
props.doc: The one hero number of a screen, set large.

props.name: samples
props.doc: Its recent readings, oldest first, as a sparkline under it.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Whether it is the selected one, when it opens a detail.

events.name: activate
events.doc: The tile was pressed: open its detail.

components.name: Stepper
components.doc: Where a person is in a short sequence: a setup wizard's steps, an import's. Each step is a station with a disc and its name; a done one carries a check and may be gone back to. Too narrow for its stations, it reads "Step 2 of 4" over the current step.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The steps, in order.

props.name: current
props.doc: Which step is current, counted from 0. None before the first step starts: every station waits.

events.name: station
events.doc: The step gone back to: carries its index. Without it, no station takes the pointer.

components.name: StrokePreview
components.doc: The mark a brush, its size and a pigment will paint, drawn as a sample stroke: a canvas's brush pad shows it before a person touches the canvas, and draws it in again when any of the three changes.

props.name: brush
props.doc: What the brush paints like: `round`, `pen`, `pencil`, `marker`, `airbrush`, `charcoal`, `calligraphy`, `eraser`, `pixel` or `pixel-eraser`; any other name paints like the round brush.

props.name: size
props.doc: How wide the brush paints, in artwork units: a width past the preview's height is drawn as tall as the preview holds.

props.name: colour
props.doc: The pigment, as `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

components.name: SunburstChart
components.doc: A hierarchy as rings: how a whole divides, and how each part divides, down to the smallest ones. Each ring is a level, a part as wide as its share of the one it belongs to, and each part takes its colour from the theme; a person pointing at one reads its path and its value.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts, each naming the part it belongs to: `.part(id: "build", parent: "ci", label: "Build", value: 12.0)`. A part nothing names as its parent stands at the centre ring.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, over it and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

props.name: total
props.doc: What the whole is, read at its centre ("128 hours"); without it the centre reads the sum of the parts, so the hole always says how large the whole is.

components.name: TabStrip
components.doc:
A frame's tabs, in one row above its content: the shell's tab strip.
The chosen tab stands lifted off the strip's ground, and every pill says who is at its resource now. Choosing a pill activates that tab; a pill's close chip closes it; dragging one within the strip reorders it, and letting one go outside the strip hands it to the frame under the pointer.

props.name: active
props.doc: The resource whose tab shows: the tab in front.

props.name: focused
props.doc: Whether this frame has the keyboard: its tab strip says so.

parts.name: tabs
parts.doc: The tabs, in order.

events.name: activate
events.doc: Told a tab was chosen: carries the resource of the pill chosen.

events.name: close
events.doc: Told a tab's close chip was pressed: carries that tab's resource.

events.name: reorder
events.doc: Told a pill was dropped at a new place in the strip: carries the tab moved and its place among the strip's, from 0.

events.name: detach
events.doc: Told a pill was dragged out of the strip and let go: carries the tab and where it was let go, as [`pack_point`] packs the window's coordinates. The shell puts the tab in the frame there, or makes one.

components.name: Terminal
components.doc:
A terminal's grid: what a running shell printed and the input that reaches it.
The window of the app, the grid and the program inside it are one thing: a terminal has no address bar, no search of its own and no chrome — the app's own window bar carries where the session runs, and find over the scrollback is the window's.

props.name: session
props.doc: The session this grid shows, as the app's record names it.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the grid shows, for assistive technology: "Terminal, Build".

props.name: copy_on_select
props.doc: Finishing a selection also copies it to the clipboard, not only to the primary selection.

props.name: bell_flash
props.doc: Flash the grid when the program rings the bell.

props.name: allow_clipboard
props.doc: Let the program put text on the clipboard (OSC 52): off unless the person allowed it.

events.name: title
events.doc: The program set the window's title.

events.name: finished
events.doc: A run the shell marked ended; carries it as JSON.

events.name: exit
events.doc: The shell exited: carries "exited", or its status.

events.name: lost
events.doc: The connection to the shell was lost: carries why.

events.name: selected
events.doc: A selection was finished: carries the text it copied.

events.name: rung
events.doc: The bell rang.

events.name: history
events.doc: The shell asked for the lines its Up recalls: carries the ask as JSON, which the app answers from the history it keeps.

events.name: held
events.doc: The session's host holds the command at the prompt until someone acts: carries why as JSON, and empty text once it let it go.

semantics.label: label
semantics.not_in_gallery: a terminal shows a shell session the window's host runs, and the gallery's window runs none

components.name: Text
components.doc: Words on the page, set in one of the design system's text roles. What it says is content, never looked up as interface copy.

props.name: value
props.doc: What it says.

props.name: role
props.doc: What the text is, which sets its size, weight and face: `body` unless said.

props.name: numeric
props.doc: A number that changes: tabular figures, so it does not jitter as it changes.

props.name: secondary
props.doc: What it says stands beside the content it is about, in secondary ink: "edited" after a message, "Pinned" over it.

props.name: lines
props.doc: How many lines it takes: what does not fit is elided at the last of them, so a clamp holds however long the words are. Unset, it wraps to as many lines as its width needs.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: It elides at the width it is given rather than wrapping wider, so its box may shrink to nothing and what does not fit ends in an ellipsis: a title in a narrow card.

props.name: live
props.doc: What it says is announced when it changes instead of only read on the way past: a line a person is told without looking (a notice passing, a status that moved). `polite` waits for a pause, `assertive` interrupts; unset, it is read without announcing.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where its lines sit across the width it is given: `start` unless said, `center` for a short message standing alone in the middle of a page.

components.name: TextInput
components.doc: A field to type text into, bound to the text it edits. Each edit is spliced into that text, never written over it, so people typing in the same text at once all keep what they typed.

props.name: text
props.doc: Text it shows when it binds nothing: read and copied, never edited (a message body, a log). A field given one is read-only; what it reports of its selection is still [`Self::select`].

props.name: read_only
props.doc: Whether it is read and copied but never edited, even when it binds a field: a value shown for reading.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: What to type, shown while it is empty.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Area for this many lines: the field wraps and grows with what is typed.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the document the window is for, edited in place as its large title.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be typed into now.

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: It is where the person types next (an entry a command just opened): it takes the keyboard as soon as it is in the window, once.

props.name: changed_by
props.doc: Someone else changed the text and the person has not seen it yet: hovering the field says who. The app's runtime sets it, from what the field is bound to (task-legibility §3).

props.name: previous
props.doc: What the text was before that change, said when the field is hovered.

props.name: entry
props.doc: The entry at the end of a list: what is typed makes an item when Enter or leaving the field commits it, and the field clears; nothing typed leaves nothing (Escape, or leaving it empty). Its own draft, not a record: the item exists once it is committed.

props.name: key
props.doc: The plain key that focuses this control while its window has the keyboard, as the app declared it (`key: "Ctrl+N"`): a window's primary action brings the person to the list's entry rather than making an empty item. Never drawn here.

props.name: caret
props.doc: A caret on a surface rather than a field in a form: no well and no fill, only as wide as what it holds, growing as the words are typed. The canvas's caret.

props.name: secret
props.doc: A secret: the field masks what it holds, never speaks or shows it in a screenshot, refuses Copy and Cut, and hands its value over only through the action it fires. For an API key or a password, where the app never reads the value back.

props.name: verbatim
props.doc: Typed exactly as it is, in the monospace face: nothing checks its spelling or corrects it. For words that must stay as written (a recovery key's, a code).

props.name: mistakes
props.doc: The runs of the text that what checks it judges wrong, underlined as a misspelling is: the start and end of each run in turn, as byte offsets into the text (a word outside the list a recovery key's words come from). A run that does not fit the text marks nothing.

events.name: submit
events.doc: Enter was pressed: what was typed is done (a list's entry), carried with it. With it, Enter ends the text rather than breaking its line; Shift+Enter still breaks a wrapping field's line.

events.name: select
events.doc: The selection settled (a drag let go, a double click, a select all, shift and an arrow key): carries the run selected as `<start>:<end>`, byte offsets into the text, or nothing when the selection collapsed. A read-only field reports it so what reads it — a message answered on just the words someone chose — can act on the run; a field being typed in keeps its selection private.

events.name: cancel
events.doc: Escape let go of what was being typed: the field clears, and what it stands in goes (a caret on the canvas).

events.name: begin
events.doc: The field's text went from empty to non-empty: the first change, carrying the text it holds now. An entry makes the item it names here, from the first keystroke.

events.name: changed
events.doc: The text changed as the person typed: carries what the field holds now. Told for every change the person makes (a key, a paste, a cut), never for what the field binds.

events.name: blur
events.doc: The field lost the keyboard: an entry left empty is taken away by what listens.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The text it edits.

components.name: TimeField
components.doc: The time of day a day is due at: the hour and the minute it is due at, with "Remove time" beside them, or a quiet "Add time" while it has none. It stands in the `time` part of a [`DateField`](crate::widget::DateField), so the day and its time read as one fact.

events.name: change
events.doc: A time was picked or removed: carries the time of day, or nothing for a removed one.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The moment, as a bound field holds it (`09:00`, or the ISO text of an instant), and where a picked time of day goes.

components.name: TimePicker
components.doc: A time of day, as spinners for hours and minutes, and for seconds when the time holds some: the arrows step a spinner and so does the wheel over its cell. It is the time in the person's own zone today.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name.

props.name: step
props.doc: The minutes the wheel and the chevrons step the minute cell by: a quarter hour by default.

events.name: changed
events.doc: The time changed: carries the instant, at the time chosen today.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: The moment, as the instant a component binds (its ISO text): today at the time chosen. A change sets the time kept in it.

components.name: Timeline
components.doc: A day, week or month as a time grid: events at their hours laid side by side where they overlap, an all-day lane, the line where now is, and a month of days with what stands on each. Dragging an event moves it, dragging its edge resizes it, and dragging across empty hours makes one that starts and ends where the drag did; each is a typed event, and the grid never changes what it shows.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the grid is, for assistive technology: "This week".

props.name: range
props.doc: The range shown: the day, the week of a day, or the month of a day.

props.name: start
props.doc: The day the period stands in.

props.name: slot
props.doc: The minutes a drag snaps to: a quarter hour by default.

props.name: show_now
props.doc: Whether the line where now is shows, read from the frame's clock (views cannot read it).

props.name: zoom
props.doc: How tall an hour is drawn against its legible minimum: 1 is the minimum, 2 twice it.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How many all-day rows the lane keeps, whatever the events need.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: What stands on the grid, in no particular order: each is placed by its own times.

events.name: created
events.doc: Empty hours were dragged across: carries where the new event starts and ends.

events.name: open_day
events.doc: A day's head was pressed: carries that day.

events.name: zoomed
events.doc: The person zoomed the hours: carries the new zoom.

components.name: Timer
components.doc: A clock the view holds: `tick` every `every` seconds, or once `after` seconds, counted from when the view first showed it.

props.name: every
props.doc: How many seconds between ticks: it ticks again and again while it is shown; 0 for a timer that ticks once.

props.name: after
props.doc: How many seconds until its one tick: it ticks once and then rests; 0 for one that ticks again and again.

props.name: restart
props.doc: What it counts from: whenever this changes, it counts again from now. A field's text here makes a timer `after` a short while tick once the person stops typing, not at every key.

events.name: tick
events.doc: Its time came.

semantics.not_in_gallery: it draws nothing: its ticks are what a view does with them

components.name: Toggle
components.doc: A switch: the same two states as a checkbox, for a setting that takes effect at once rather than when a form is sent. Its knob slides to the side it turns to.

props.name: shown
props.doc: Whether it is on, for a view that reads the state rather than binding a place of its own: the switch shows it and turns only through its event, so a change from elsewhere shows when the view is drawn again.

props.name: label
props.doc: The setting's name, beside the switch at the row's leading edge: the whole row turns it, and assistive technology reads it with the state.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be turned now.

events.name: check
events.doc: It was turned: whether it is on now, in the app's words.

bindings.name: value
bindings.doc: Whether it is on, and where a turn of it goes.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.doc: A small set of choices, one of which is made: an alignment, a density, a unit. The chosen one is a thumb lifted off the track.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Which choice is made, counted from 0: none until the person makes one.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A label over the strip naming what it chooses between.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name, for a strip its caption does not name.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large its segments are: `regular` unless said.

props.name: fill
props.doc: Share the row's width equally instead of fitting each label.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be chosen from now.

parts.name: options
parts.doc: The choices, in order.

events.name: change
events.doc: A choice was made: carries the index of the chosen option, counted from 0.

components.name: ViewTabs
components.doc: Tabs that switch what a window's content shows: a request's Params, Headers and Body, a container's Logs and Stats. Assistive technology meets them as a tab list whose chosen tab is selected, not checked.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Which tab shows, counted from 0.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its spoken name for assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.doc: How large the tabs are: `regular` unless said.

props.name: fill
props.doc: Share the row's width equally instead of fitting each label.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether it can be chosen from now.

parts.name: tabs
parts.doc: The tabs, in order.

events.name: change
events.doc: Another tab was chosen: carries its index, counted from 0.

components.name: Toolbar
components.doc: A strip of commands: plain buttons in a row, groups split by hairlines, toggles that stand lifted while on. However narrow the window, every command stays reachable: those that do not fit go to a More menu at the end, the least important first.

props.name: vertical
props.doc: Stand the commands in a column rather than a row.

parts.name: items
parts.doc: Its commands, separators and spacers, in order.

components.name: TrackTimeline
components.doc: A time ruler over rows of tracks, with what stands on each track as spans, the markers a person set on the ruler and the playhead: a film's cut, a sound's layers, a show's timing. Dragging a span moves it along its track or onto another, dragging its edge trims it, and both line up with the grid, the other spans' edges, the markers and the playhead; dragging along the ruler moves the playhead. The wheel and a pinch zoom the lane about the pointer and scroll it along the time, and a bar under the tracks shows how much of the cut the lane holds and moves it. Each is a typed event, and the timeline never changes what it shows: the view commits the change, and the span settles into the place the view gives it.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the timeline is, for assistive technology: "The cut".

props.name: span
props.doc: How many seconds the lane shows across its width: the zoom.

props.name: scroll
props.doc: The moment the lane's leading edge shows.

props.name: playhead
props.doc: Where the playhead stands, in seconds.

props.name: length
props.doc: How long what is on the tracks runs, in seconds: where zooming to fit and the end key go.

props.name: clips
props.doc: The moments a measurement found a problem at — where the mix went over full scale — marked on the ruler and down the tracks, so the flag stands where it happened.

props.name: step
props.doc: The grid a drag lands on, in seconds: one frame (1/30) for a film, nothing for free time.

props.name: enabled
props.doc: Whether a press on a track runs now.

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, where the label does not say (an action whose requirement does not hold): spoken as its description beside its name.

parts.name: tracks
parts.doc: The tracks, top to bottom, each with what stands on it.

parts.name: markers
parts.doc: The moments marked on the ruler.

events.name: scrub
events.doc: The playhead is being dragged: carries where it is now, as the hand moves.

events.name: seek
events.doc: The playhead was set down: the ruler pressed, the playhead let go, or a key moved it. Carries where it stands.

events.name: zoomed
events.doc: The person zoomed: carries how many seconds the lane shows now.

events.name: scrolled
events.doc: The person scrolled along the time: carries the moment the leading edge shows now.

events.name: press
events.doc: A track's empty stretch was pressed: carries the moment and the track's key.

components.name: TreeView
components.doc: A tree of nodes: a file explorer, a project's files, the layers of a drawing, a book's pages. Each node is the resource it stands for; opening a branch shows the nodes under it, and selecting or activating a node reports its resource.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the tree is, for assistive technology.

props.name: fill
props.doc: The tree takes the height it is given and scrolls inside itself, rather than sizing to the rows inside another scroll. Such a tree is the pane's list, so its rows stand on the pane's content edge (where the pane's header starts its title) with their lift bleeding past it, as every list in a column does — including a phone's window, where the pane is the whole screen and the rows keep the page gutter at its glass.

props.name: hide_root
props.doc: The tree's root node — the tree itself, labelled with its `name` — is not a row: the nodes at the top level are, at the first depth. Off, the tree's name stands over them as a row of its own.

props.name: single_click
props.doc: A press selects and activates in one, as a navigator sidebar does; a double click activates otherwise.

props.name: selection_follows_focus
props.doc: Moving through the rows with the keyboard selects them as it goes.

props.name: multi_select
props.doc: Whether several nodes may be selected at once (Ctrl-click, Shift-click).

props.name: reorder
props.doc: Rows move: by dragging one onto another (before it, inside it or after it), and by `Tab` and `Shift-Tab` to indent and outdent, `Alt-Up` and `Alt-Down` to reorder among siblings. A move is reported by the node it lands at ([`TreeViewNodeProps::drop`], [`TreeViewNodeProps::into`]) or, at the top level's end, by the tree's [`Self::drop`].

props.name: tab_indents
props.doc: `Tab` and `Shift-Tab` indent and outdent the focused row. On by itself with [`Self::reorder`]; off, `Tab` moves the focus on as it otherwise would.

props.name: motion
props.doc: The pace its own motion plays at: branches unfolding, rows arriving and leaving. Unset, the theme's.

parts.name: nodes
parts.doc: The nodes, in order, parents before their children.

parts.name: removed
parts.doc: The rows in place of nodes someone else removed that the person has not seen go: they stand after the nodes, struck, each with its mark. The UI host places them.

events.name: select
events.doc: A node was selected: carries the resource it shows.

events.name: activate
events.doc: A node was activated (a double click, Enter, an assistive technology): carries the resource it shows.

events.name: drop
events.doc: A row was dropped just before another, or moved there by the keyboard: carries the row that moved and the row it lands before — none for the end of the top level.

events.name: into
events.doc: A row was dropped inside another, at the end of its own, or indented there by the keyboard: carries the row that moved and the row it lands inside — none for the end of the top level, which stands inside no row.

events.name: after
events.doc: A row was dropped just after another and all that stands under it, or moved there by the keyboard: carries the row that moved and the row it lands after. The view places it past that row's own, which only the view can name: what stands under them are rows the tree may not have built.

state.name: expanded
state.doc: The nodes open now, by the resource each stands for. Given, it is where the view says the tree is; without it the tree keeps what a person opened.

state.name: matching
state.doc: The rows a search found, by the resource each stands for, when the tree shows what the search narrowed it to: the rows the tree shows that are not among them stand for where the found ones are, and read in the quietest ink. None, every row is one the tree shows for itself.

state.name: selection
state.doc: The nodes selected, by the resource each stands for.

components.name: Treemap
components.doc: A hierarchy as rectangles: each part of the first level a rectangle as large as its share of the whole, its label written on it where it fits, in a colour from the theme. Use it where labels have to be read, rather than followed round a ring.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts, each naming the part it belongs to: `.part(id: "build", parent: "ci", label: "Build", value: 12.0)`. A part nothing names as its parent is a rectangle of its own, as large as everything under it.

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows, over it and as assistive technology announces it.

props.name: empty
props.doc: What it says while it has nothing to show, and why: "No request has been answered yet". Without it the chart says only that it has nothing to show.

components.name: VideoPlayer
components.doc:
A video with its playback controls over it: play/pause, the scrubber, the volume, mute and fullscreen. The app's player is the one truth; what the person does reaches the view as its events.
The video's bytes are a camera, a capture, or the medium it names (a file or a stream), which the toolkit opens on the engine its app hands in.

props.name: title
props.doc: The video's title, for assistive technology.

props.name: poster
props.doc: A still shown before the first frame: a picture by its address.

props.name: playing
props.doc: Whether it plays.

props.name: position
props.doc: Where it is, in seconds.

props.name: duration
props.doc: How long it is, in seconds.

props.name: seek_to
props.doc: Jump here, in seconds: a one-shot control, applied when `seek_to_seq` changes, so a bookmark's jump, a restart or a jump to the end reaches the player once and the resting `position` never fights the `progress` reading.

props.name: seek_to_seq
props.doc: Counts the view's jumps: a number it raises each time it asks to jump.

props.name: source
props.doc: Where it is stored, as a `file://` address or a URL the engine fetches.

props.name: volume
props.doc: The volume, `0..=1`.

props.name: muted
props.doc: Whether it is muted.

props.name: rate
props.doc: The speed it plays at, `0.25..=4`; absent at normal speed.

props.name: live
props.doc: Whether the source airs as it plays (an HLS or DASH manifest): the player says where it stands is live and a jump goes to the live edge rather than to a place in a recording.

props.name: qualities
props.doc: The qualities it offers to pick from, best first; empty when it has no choice.

props.name: playing_quality
props.doc: The quality it plays at, as one of `qualities`; empty takes the first.

props.name: caption_tracks
props.doc: The caption tracks it offers, by the language code each is in: the label the menu shows.

props.name: caption_language
props.doc: The language code of the track whose words are shown; empty turns captions off.

props.name: captions
props.doc: The words of the chosen track, as the WebVTT document it is: drawn over the picture as the playhead reaches each cue.

props.name: repeat
props.doc: Whether it begins again when it ends.

props.name: audio_track
props.doc: The audio track by its index in `audio_tracks`; absent leaves the engine's choice.

props.name: subtitle_track
props.doc: The subtitle track by its index in `subtitle_tracks`; `-1` turns subtitles off.

events.name: set_playing
events.doc: Play or pause was pressed: carries `true` when it plays.

events.name: seek
events.doc: It was moved to a place in the video: carries `0..=1`.

events.name: set_volume
events.doc: The volume was set: carries `0..=1`.

events.name: set_rate
events.doc: A speed was chosen: carries it, as `1.0` is normal.

events.name: select_quality
events.doc: A quality was chosen: carries its label, one of `qualities`.

events.name: select_captions
events.doc: A caption track was chosen: carries its language code, empty for off.

events.name: fail
events.doc: The player could not show its video: carries what the engine said, and where in the video it stopped, in seconds. A stream a source serves only partway through stops here, and the app asks the source for a fresh address and continues from that place.

events.name: progress
events.doc: Where playback got to while it played, as a share of its length (`0..=1`): reported on the first frame it plays, then every five seconds, and once more when it stops, so a view remembers the place a video was left at even when nobody moved the playhead.

events.name: length
